title: OPERATION GLASS GIANT
skeleton: garrison must spend an irreplaceable deterrent machine's finite working life in public displays to keep a raid from ever landing, while every display wears the machine toward the day the bluff is real and every cancellation feeds the rumor that it already is
inspiration: Tirpitz in the Norwegian fjords — fleet-in-being doctrine, 1942-44
situation:
{WORLD} dropped off the Republic's records in 3135, when the Fortress wall was raised 80 light-years coreward and the Republic garrison pulled out on 11 days' notice. Left behind: a planetary militia of 2 motorized rifle battalions, 1 armor company with 9 Vedette tanks, and the Pillar of {WORLD} — an Atlas AS7-D assault 'Mech, its hull plates dated 2989, that stood as a memorial for 40 years until a cooperative of 22 retired technicians got it running again in 3137. Since its first anniversary parade, raiders have steered clear of the system. In two years they hit four neighboring systems and left {WORLD} alone. This comes from courier news digests 19 to 66 days old, so treat it as likely but not certain. {EMPLOYER} — the planetary assembly's defense committee, acting through {NPC:employer-contact} — believes the Pillar is what keeps raiders away. They have hired your unit to garrison the world and run the deterrent program.

The problem is that the Atlas is wearing out and cannot be replaced. The technicians certify {PARTS_HOURS} walking-hours of life left in its original hip and gyro assemblies. The one factory that could supply replacement parts has not answered any message in 14 years. Every public parade burns some of that remaining life. But those same parades are what keep raiders away. Now a rumor is spreading, first heard at the spaceport 9 weeks ago from an unknown source. It says the Pillar is a gutted shell with no working parts, hauled around at night on a flatbed truck to fake that it still walks. The committee wants that rumor killed by staging the longest parade in the program's history.

The key terrain problem is the sluice bridge. The only direct route from the memorial vault to the spaceport plain crosses this bridge, which was rated to carry 95 tons in 3102 and has never been re-inspected since. The Atlas weighs 100 tons — over the limit. So every parade must instead take the long way, the Ring Route: 26 kilometers through the capital's streets, 4 hours at parade pace, every step of it burning the 'Mech's limited service life and on public display the whole way.

One more item in the digest, and this one is 31 days old and unconfirmed: a tramp freighter captain says someone questioned him in detail about {WORLD}'s parade schedule, in a spaceport bar 2 jumps away. {NPC:intel-source} confirms the man asking paid in raider scrip. Someone is checking whether the deterrent is real. Pirates do not investigate a threat they mean to keep avoiding.

objectives.primary: Keep the deterrent working. No enemy force lands on {WORLD} during the contract year, and the public keeps believing the Pillar is real.
objectives.secondary: Add life to the Atlas. Find, build, or re-engineer hip and gyro parts that add at least 100 walking-hours to its service life.
objectives.bonus: Find out who is behind the off-world questions and the flatbed rumor, with proof the defense committee can act on.

complications.name: The Service-Life Ledger
complications.text: The Atlas's hip and gyro assemblies have {PARTS_HOURS} walking-hours of life left, and no replacement parts exist within 2 jumps. Only 6 people know the real number. If it leaks to the enemy, they will know exactly how long the deterrent can last and simply wait it out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every time the Pillar moves, hours come off a tracked service-life pool. Parade pace burns 1 hour for each hour walked. Combat pace burns 3. When the pool hits zero, the Atlas can no longer walk and is just a statue. If the real number leaks, the enemy stops guessing and times its raid for the day the deterrent runs out.

complications.name: The Enemy's Observers
complications.text: {SPOTTERS} off-world observers have been seen working the parade route with professional cameras and sensors. Arresting them as spies without proof causes a scandal. But whatever they are allowed to see decides whether raiders think the world is worth attacking.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Hostile observers watch every public event. Their verdict on the deterrent sets how likely raids are for the whole campaign year: CREDIBLE, HOLLOW, or UNCERTAIN. The player's choices at the decision points below shape that verdict.

complications.name: Re-Rating the Sluice Bridge
complications.text: An engineering survey could re-inspect the sluice bridge and maybe clear it for the Atlas's weight. That would cut the parade route from 26 kilometers to 9. The survey costs 40,000 C-bills and takes 30 days. But it might find the bridge can bear only 90 tons, less than the Atlas's 100, and rule it out for good.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until a survey is paid for and passes, every Pillar move must use the 26 km Ring Route and burns the full service-life cost. If the survey fails, the short route is closed to the Atlas for good, and the bridge's real weight limit becomes public.

decisionPoints.name: The Anniversary Parade
decisionPoints.context: The committee wants the longest parade in the program's history, 18 days from now, to kill the flatbed rumor. But every step the Atlas takes burns service life that can never be replaced, so there is pressure to keep it standing still. The enemy's observers will be watching whatever the unit decides to do.

options.title: Full Ring Parade
advantages: The strongest answer to the rumor: a full 26-kilometer walk, no flatbed in sight
Committee relations and militia morale both peak
The enemy's observers have to report an Atlas that really walks
disadvantages: Burns 4.5 hours of service life that cannot be refilled
26 kilometers of close observation lets skilled analysts spot and measure the worn left hip
One stumble in public would end the whole program in an afternoon
options.consequence: The rumor dies for a season, and the 'Mech is a season closer to wearing out. The observers report what they saw. If their sensors are good enough, that includes the limp in the left hip around kilometer 19, which tells them the machine is damaged.

costs.resource: Pillar service life: 4.5 walking-hours out of the {PARTS_HOURS} remaining
costs.risk: close observation of the worn hip lets the enemy measure how damaged the 'Mech is. That is almost as bad as leaking the real service-life number.

options.title: Stationary Live-Fire Display
advantages: A firing demonstration from the memorial concourse: engine running, weapons live. It proves the 'Mech works and burns only 0.5 hours of service life instead of 4.5.
Controlled ground: observers see only what the unit chooses to stage
disadvantages: Half the crowd reads an Atlas that only stands still as an Atlas that cannot walk, so the rumor changes shape instead of dying
Spends live ammunition on a world that cannot resupply it
options.consequence: The display proves the 'Mech works but not that it can move. The rumor changes from 'gutted shell' to 'frozen knees,' and the committee's next demand will be a walking parade anyway.

costs.resource: Pillar service life: 0.5 walking-hours, plus one reload of AC/20 and LRM ammunition that cannot be replaced locally
costs.risk: the display answers the wrong question. The enemy wants to know whether the 'Mech can move, not whether it can shoot.

options.title: Cancel the Parade and Plant an Overhaul Cover Story
advantages: Spends zero service life during the most closely watched month of the program
A planted cover story gives the cancellation a respectable reason: staged photos at the maintenance dock, parts crates, technician interviews
Buys 34 days of doubt in the enemy's mind, the time for word to travel out and back
disadvantages: On the planet, cancelling the parade looks like proof the rumor is true, whatever the press release says
The cover story has to travel by courier to the spaceports where raiders gather. That takes 34 days, and the enemy's observers may file their report first.
options.consequence: The 'Mech is preserved, but the bluff is now on borrowed time. If the cover story arrives first, the observers report UNCERTAIN and raiders stay away. If their report arrives first, {WORLD} has just confirmed it backed down.

costs.resource: 34 days to spread the cover story through 3 neighboring spaceports. The deterrent is on borrowed time until the story lands.
costs.risk: a race between the planted story and the enemy's report, run at courier speed, with the whole planet as the prize

decisionPoints.name: What to Do About the Observers
decisionPoints.context: Counterintelligence has pinned down {SPOTTERS} observers at the overlook above the route junction, equipped with sensors and a transmitter to send their findings off-world. They have broken no law on {WORLD}'s books.

options.title: Arrest and Interrogate Them
advantages: The only option that can directly identify who hired the observers
Removes professional observers from the parade route before the anniversary
disadvantages: Arresting foreign nationals on mere suspicion hurts the committee's standing in public
The arrest is itself a tell: whoever hired the observers learns {WORLD} is nervous enough to detain visitors
Replacement observers arrive within about a month, better prepared
options.consequence: Maybe some names and a lead to whoever is behind this, and a guarantee that the next observers will be harder to spot. Either way, the committee is left with a diplomatic incident.

costs.resource: committee standing: a public arrest with no actual crime to charge
costs.risk: interrogation yields only a middleman's name, while the person behind it learns the deterrent's keepers panicked first

options.title: Put On a Show Aimed at Them
advantages: Deterrence aimed straight at the decision-makers: route the parade through the junction at combat pace, then finish with a live-fire demonstration at the river range
If the performance is flawless, the observers can only report that the deterrent is real
disadvantages: Combat pace burns service life at triple the normal rate
A show staged for hostile sensors is also judged by them. One visible fault and they report the 'Mech is damaged.
options.consequence: The observers get the show they came for. Their report will say either CREDIBLE or HOLLOW, with no middle ground, and the 'Mech's service life pays for that certainty either way.

costs.resource: Pillar service life: 11 walking-hours at combat pace, plus live-fire ammunition
costs.risk: under professional sensors, a single actuator fault tells the enemy the deterrent is weak and marks the world as a target

options.title: Feed Them the Flatbed Rumor
advantages: Let the observers photograph a staged night move of a draped fake 'Mech, then walk the real Pillar past their lodgings at dawn
Ruins the enemy's trust in every report they have ever had from {WORLD}, past and future
disadvantages: 16 days of prep, and a fake that has to survive professional scrutiny
If the fake is spotted, the unit has confirmed it plays tricks. The enemy then escalates to a probe in force, on the logic that only a weak deterrent needs deception.
options.consequence: Done cleanly, the enemy's spying on {WORLD} is worthless for a year: every future rumor arrives already doubted. Done badly, the enemy stops spying and sends a 'Mech lance to test the deterrent in person.

costs.resource: fabrication-shop time and the counterintelligence team's only deception asset, spent in one go
costs.risk: if the fake is caught, doubt turns into provocation. That is the one outcome worse than a report that the deterrent is hollow.

entries.event: The ground watch spots an unscheduled ship burning in on a descent. The size fits one Union-class DropShip. It runs no transponder. The alarm goes out by landline.
Militia called up: rifle battalions to their district assembly points, the Vedette tank company to the spaceport plain.
The Pillar starts its cold start in the concourse vault. Walk-out is {COLD_START} hours away. Main-gun ammunition trucks in from the arsenal 11 km away, as the law requires.
Earliest the Pillar can walk out, on the Ring Route, at its best steady pace.
Earliest the enemy could land if the descent holds. The likely landing window runs to T+14:00.
The Pillar reaches the spaceport plain, in plain view from every approach.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The deterrent only works if the enemy sees it in time. The Pillar must be standing in plain view on the spaceport plain before the intruder commits to its final descent, which is likely between T+9:00 and T+14:00. Miss that window and deterrence has failed. Then {WORLD}'s defense is a real battle: 2 rifle battalions, 9 Vedette tanks, and one Atlas with {PARTS_HOURS} hours of service life left, fighting alone, with no working HPG to call for help or even report what happened.

opforSketch.composition: A pirate consortium that scouts a target before committing to a raid. Scouting tier: hired civilian observers (Green, unarmed). Raid tier, committed only if the observers judge {WORLD}'s deterrent to be hollow: 6-10 salvage-grade 'Mechs (Green/Regular), supporting technicals, 1-2 Union-class DropShips. The generator should scale the raid strictly to the observers' verdict: CREDIBLE brings no raid, UNCERTAIN brings a probing lance, HOLLOW brings the full consortium.
opforSketch.behavior: Patient and businesslike. They are not raiding {WORLD} yet; they are assessing whether it is worth raiding. Probing elements withdraw the moment they see a credible assault-'Mech and come back to reassess next year. The full consortium, once committed, fights for the spaceport and the grain stores rather than for honor, and lifts off the moment the raid stops being profitable.

forks.name: OPERATION DEEP SPARE
forks.trigger: The contract year ends with no enemy landings and the Atlas's service life still above 60 hours.
forks.consequence: The committee votes funds for the only permanent fix: an expedition to the silent factory world that last answered a message 14 years ago. The goal is to recover hip and gyro parts from whoever holds it now. The unit escorts the mission to secure the deterrent's future.

forks.name: OPERATION CALLED BLUFF
forks.trigger: The enemy's observers conclude the deterrent is HOLLOW, or the true service-life figure leaks, and a raid force lands.
forks.consequence: The deterrent must finally do the one thing it was kept in reserve to avoid: fight. The Pillar fights with whatever service life it has left, in front of the population that believed in it. Every hour it fights now is an hour taken from every year to come.

forks.name: OPERATION FLATBED
forks.trigger: The deception is exposed, or the Atlas's true service-life figure reaches the arms-broker network.
forks.consequence: The enemy stops spying and starts bidding. A brokered offer of 2.2 million C-bills for the Atlas arrives by mail packet. It splits the assembly between those who want to sell the bluff and those who want to keep it. The unit now has to guard the Pillar against its own would-be sellers.

storyElementSeed: Parade morning. A tech with forty years of grease in his knuckles chalks a number on the inside of the left hip access panel where no crowd will ever see it. The number is smaller than it was in spring.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Put On a Show Aimed at Them
resourceGates.lackingText: No munitions depot under contract, so the live-fire ammunition must be bought on the open market. Add 14,000 C-bills. The purchase order itself is visible to anyone watching the spaceport's cargo records.
No secure workshop, so the fake 'Mech must be built in a rented civilian shop. Add 6 days. Every extra worker who helps build it is one more person who could leak the secret.

title: OPERATION QUIET ARSENAL
skeleton: garrison hired to disarm a world must decide whose law it is enforcing while the confiscated garage arsenal is the only thing that stops the raids and the authority behind the writ may have lapsed with the government that issued it
inspiration: Inter-Allied disarmament commissions and the Freikorps weapon caches, Weimar Germany 1920-23
situation:
{WORLD} was disarmed by Republic decree in 3084. The militia was dissolved, its BattleMechs were bought back, and the planetary arsenal was melted down at the smelters. A public holiday marked the day. But the decree has outlived the government that issued it. The Blackout killed the HPG in 3132. The Fortress wall cut off the Republic in 3135. The prefect who governs {WORLD} now holds a post that no living authority can renew. He governs out of habit from a half-empty tower, and 60 percent of the planetary assembly has stopped attending his sessions. That figure comes from the assembly clerk's attendance roll, 11 days old and reliable.

What the decree could not melt down was the machine shops. Over the past 19 months, 14 licensed farm-equipment shops have built {CONVERSIONS} armed IndustrialMech conversions: MiningMechs with an autocannon bolted where the drill used to be, AgroMechs carrying salvaged missile racks. Tax informants say more were built illegally, but no one will put a number on it. Two raids hit the outlying districts in the past 5 months. Both were driven off by these conversions, not by the prefecture's 120-officer police force.

{EMPLOYER} is the prefect's office, acting through {NPC:employer-contact}. It has hired your unit to enforce the 3084 decree: seize the conversions into a central armory under the prefecture's control. The legal authority for this is a Republic law, but the Republic is now unreachable. Asking the nearest working Republic office whether the decree still stands takes one full courier round trip, {COURIER_LOOP} days, and the honest answer is that no one will likely reply at all. So the contract rests on an authority that cannot be confirmed, and everyone on {WORLD} knows it.

The key terrain problem is the rail defile. The valley holds 9 of the 14 shops and is the heart of the resistance, which calls itself the Implement Combine. One rail line connects the valley to the capital plain through the defile: 7 kilometers of cut granite, 2 sidings, and no parallel road for 60 kilometers. Every confiscation convoy, every parts shipment, and every response to a valley raid has to use that one line. The Combine knows it. Its track-maintenance vehicles now carry welded armor plate and weapon mounts, and {NPC:intel-source} reports the Combine drills derailment and recovery on the second Sunday of every month, practicing to block the line.

objectives.primary: Settle the arsenal question across all 14 shops without starting a civil war. Do it either by the employer's writ or by a new registration deal the employer co-signs.
objectives.secondary: Keep every outlying district within 4 hours of an armed response through raid season. No district goes undefended while its machines sit crated on railcars.
objectives.bonus: Get one solid ruling on the prefect's authority before the contract ends: a reply from a Republic office, an assembly vote to ratify, or a formal abdication.

complications.name: The Unconfirmable Decree
complications.text: The law being enforced is 52 years old, and the government that made it is unreachable behind the Fortress wall. Every weapon seized by force reopens the same public argument: does the prefect even have the authority to seize it? Here, that argument gets settled at gunpoint.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every enforcement action taken by force rolls against a planetary legitimacy track. That track decides which factions cooperate, which shops comply on their own, and whether the assembly will ratify anything the unit negotiates.

complications.name: Raid Season
complications.text: Two raids in 5 months, both driven off by the converted farm 'Mechs. The raiders follow the confiscation news as closely as everyone else does. To them, each newly disarmed district is a target that just lost its guns.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Confiscated machines in transit or in armory storage cannot defend anything. Raids hit the district with the least armed coverage at that moment. Each raid that lands on a disarmed district shifts the legitimacy track against the employer.

complications.name: The Combine's Railway
complications.text: Nine shops, one rail line, two sidings, and members who have built armed rail vehicles and practice blocking the line every month. Holding the defile is the Combine's main bargaining chip.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All rail movement through the defile needs an escort. Combine sabotage can close the line for 2 to 5 days. While it is closed, the valley can only be reached by air or by a 60 km cross-country march.

decisionPoints.name: Whose Law to Enforce
decisionPoints.context: The contract says to enforce the decree. The decree's authority is the Republic. The Republic has said nothing for years and cannot be reached. The unit has to decide what authority it is actually acting on before the Combine forces the question.

options.title: Enforce the Decree as Written
advantages: Follows the contract exactly, with no improvising, so the fee is secure
Gathers every armed machine under one command and one armory
The prefect's authority looks real for as long as the unit backs it with force
disadvantages: Hands all the planet's weapons to the prefect, the man with the weakest claim to legitimacy
Resistance from the valley is almost certain, and the Combine controls the defile
Disarms the only force that has actually beaten raiders, right at the start of raid season
options.consequence: The decree survives another year, enforced at gunpoint. The armory fills up, the districts are left undefended, and the question of who legitimately governs simply passes to whoever takes over next, possibly the raiders.

costs.resource: legitimacy: every weapon seized by force is a recruiting argument for the Combine
costs.risk: raid season arrives to find the planet's only working defense crated up at Siding 2, with the unit's name on the shipping manifest

options.title: Switch to a Register-and-License Scheme
advantages: Keeps the armed 'Mechs spread out where the raids actually fall. Assessment says 11 of the 14 shops will comply willingly.
Turns the unit from a confiscator into an inspector, a job one lance can handle instead of a battalion
The assembly will ratify it, which is the closest thing to law {WORLD} can currently make
disadvantages: The employer may call this a breach of contract, since his own contractor publicly weakens his authority
Registering the conversions legally also makes the Combine's weapons and its politics legitimate
options.consequence: {WORLD} gets a militia under a different name, and the prefect gets a precedent he will not like: his own contractor rewriting planetary law in his name. The fee survives in a renegotiated form. His office may not.

costs.resource: the employer's standing: his own contractor publicly rewriting his decree
costs.risk: a breach-of-contract claim against the unit's bond if the prefect rejects the new scheme after the shops have already complied

options.title: Suspend Enforcement and Verify the Authority
advantages: Hard to attack: freeze enforcement, send a courier to ask the nearest Republic office, and hold things as they are until an answer comes back
Whatever comes back, whether the decree is renewed, cancelled, or met with silence, is the only real authority anyone will have seen in years
disadvantages: {COURIER_LOOP} days of paid idleness while the Combine digs in and raid season starts
The prefect treats the freeze as mutiny dressed up as paperwork
The most likely answer is silence, which settles nothing and leaves the question even older
options.consequence: The unit buys a real answer, but at Dark-Age speed. For one full courier round trip, {WORLD}'s arsenal question stays open while everyone watches the mail. The raiders keep to no schedule but their own.

costs.resource: one courier round trip ({COURIER_LOOP} days) of limbo, paid for in raid-season exposure
costs.risk: the most likely reply is no reply, leaving the same question even older, with the Combine dug in by then

decisionPoints.name: Dealing With the Combine
decisionPoints.context: The Combine has answered in writing: the 9 valley shops will not hand their machines to an official whose authority cannot be proven. The letter is polite. Its armed rail vehicles are not.

options.title: Take the Valley by Force
advantages: Breaks the organized resistance before it hardens into a rival government
Fast: finished before raid season peaks, with the armory gathered up afterward
The other 5 shops fall in line the same week, guaranteed
disadvantages: Casualties among the very people who fought off the last raid
Leaves the defile behind a hostile population, so every future convoy is a fight waiting to happen
If the Republic later rules the prefect's authority invalid, this was armed robbery backed by rail power
options.consequence: The valley falls in days and stays fallen only as long as the unit personally garrisons it. {WORLD}'s only experienced fighters are now either its prisoners or its insurgents.

costs.resource: the defile: taken once by assault, then held forever against the people who live there
costs.risk: fighting the planet's only proven raid-defense during raid season, on the strength of an authority nobody can prove

options.title: Blockade the Defile
advantages: Bloodless: control the rail line, ration the parts traffic, and let the pressure build
The Combine's converted 'Mechs need spare parts the valley cannot make itself
Leaves every exit open for a negotiated registration deal
disadvantages: The capital depends on valley grain, so the blockade cuts both ways within {GRAIN_DAYS} days
A siege that drags on for months favors raid season and rumor
options.consequence: Supply pressure does the fighting instead of guns. The winner is whichever side runs short last. But the capital's grain countdown is public knowledge, while the Combine's parts stockpile is not.

costs.resource: the capital's grain reserve: {GRAIN_DAYS} days at current rations before the blockade starves the unit's own employer
costs.risk: a siege that may starve the besieger first, run in full view of raiders watching for undefended districts

options.title: Deputize the Combine
advantages: Maximum raid coverage at no cost: swear the converted 'Mechs in as auxiliary district militia under the unit's command
The fight disappears, because the Combine wanted official standing, not war
Registration in everything but name
disadvantages: Openly reverses the contract: the unit hired to seize the weapons now commands them
The prefect's office may stop payment and seize the unit's bond
The 5 shops that complied ask, fairly, why refusing earned the Combine a better deal than obeying did
options.consequence: {WORLD} gets a real defense force this season, commanded by the unit and owing nothing to the prefect. Whoever holds the contract next inherits a militia the government did not create and cannot disband.

costs.resource: the employer's remaining authority, spent by his own contractor with one signature
costs.risk: both the fee and the bond ride on whether the prefect accepts this rather than call it the breach it is

entries.event: Raid alarm at the {DISTRICT} grain elevators, called in by landline from the elevator watch. {DISTRICT}'s 4 conversions sit crated on railcars at Siding 2, seized 6 days ago.
The {DISTRICT} police post formally asks for the crated machines to be released to their former crews.
The Combine offers 6 of its own machines, armed, unregistered, 70 minutes out by rail. The condition: a written amnesty signed by the unit commander.
Raiders finish sweeping the perimeter and start loading grain, the same pattern they used in the previous 2 strikes.
Raiders finish looting and lift off. This timing is based on both prior strikes and is likely, not certain.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: By T+3:00 the unit must do one of three things: release the seized machines back to the crews it took them from, accept the Combine's armed help on the Combine's written terms, or fight the raid alone with whatever it can move through the defile in time. At T+7:00 the grain elevators are empty. If the unit has not chosen by then, the delay itself is the choice, made in public, during raid season, with the legitimacy track recording the result.

opforSketch.composition: Raider element: a light salvage company — 4-6 'Mech-scale machines of mixed grade (Green/Regular), armed technicals, one Buccaneer-class lifter. Local armed parties: the Combine's {CONVERSIONS}-strong conversion pool (Green crews, home ground, improvised machines with real guns). Generator should treat the Combine as a faction that can appear on either side of any engagement depending on the legitimacy track, never as a fixed OPFOR.
opforSketch.behavior: Raiders avoid armed districts and strike undefended gaps within 10-20 days of any publicized confiscation; they fight only long enough to break contact and escape. The Combine fights defensively and only on or near its own valley ground — with one exception: it will always answer a raid alarm anywhere on {WORLD}, because every alarm it answers is proof that its 'Mechs, not the prefect's police, are what keeps the planet safe.

forks.name: OPERATION STANDING WRIT
forks.trigger: The assembly ratifies a registration scheme with the prefect's co-signature, and raid season ends without losing a district.
forks.consequence: {WORLD} passes its first law of the post-Republic era and hires the unit to run the inspection scheme it wrote — wardens to train, registries to audit, and 14 shops now building to a legal standard the unit certifies.

forks.name: OPERATION FREE VALLEY
forks.trigger: The valley is taken by force without a ruling on the prefect's authority, or the blockade starves the capital first.
forks.consequence: The Combine declares the valley independent, the defile becomes a contested border, and the prefect demands the unit retake it under a contract clause written for riot control. The unit must choose between fighting that campaign and forfeiting its bond.

forks.name: OPERATION PAPER THRONE
forks.trigger: The Republic's reply arrives and cancels the prefect's authority — or confirms it after the unit has already rewritten his decree.
forks.consequence: Two governments now claim {WORLD}: the prefect by habit, and the assembly by ratification. Pay is frozen pending the answer to a question the contract never anticipated, and both claimants want the unit's garrison presence as their endorsement.

storyElementSeed: In a shed that smells of cut barley, a welder grinds the registration number off a mining rig's torso plate, then stamps a new one half a digit at a time. The number format is from a militia dissolved before she was born.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Suspend Enforcement and Verify the Authority
resourceGates.lackingText: The courier fee must be taken on credit at double rate: 18,000 C-bills charged against the contract's final payment. The captain holds the reply until the balance is paid.
No fixed rail garrison, so the blockade has to run from leased rail vehicles. Add 6,000 C-bills per month. The lease records can be read by any clerk friendly with the Combine.

title: OPERATION PAPER ANCHOR
skeleton: security detail must hold an isolated waystation against a rival claimant whose ownership paperwork cannot be verified faster than the standoff can escalate, while the station's neutrality — the thing both claimants want to own — is destroyed by the first shot either side fires
inspiration: post-Soviet reiderstvo — armed corporate registry raids, Russia 1990s; lighthouse-keeper isolation posts
situation:
The anchorage sits at the {WORLD} zenith jump point. It is a recharge station and a cargo transfer ring. Since the Blackout, it is also the unofficial mail hub for 5 systems. Courier JumpShips swap mailbags, passengers, and bonded cargo here on a circuit nobody planned but everybody now depends on. There are 5 such ships, and {CONVERGENCE_DAY} days until the next quarterly convergence brings all of them to dock within the same 60-hour window. Your unit holds the station's security contract from its legal owner, the Tyrell Combine, a family freight firm two generations old. Their man aboard is {NPC:employer-contact}, the resident stationmaster.

Nineteen days ago a chartered Mule freighter docked at the far ring. It carried {MERIDIAN_GUARDS} personnel of the Meridian Custodial Group, a licensed private security company, not a mercenary unit. They came with crowd-control gear, corporate manners, and lawyers' letters. Their cargo is paperwork: deeds claiming the Combine's core-side heirs sold the anchorage 14 months ago. The registry that would prove or disprove the deeds is inside Fortress Republic and cannot be reached by any means that now exist. The stationmaster says the deeds are forged; the Meridian site director says the stationmaster is a holdover squatting on his client's property. Since docking, Meridian has posted 'joint custody' guards at 2 of the station's junctions, adding one guard post at a time, each move too small to fight over.

The key terrain problem is the Spine. It is an 800-meter central corridor linking the reactor, the sail control, and the dock ring. It is the only pressurized passage that runs the whole length of the station. Three valve junctions along the Spine control power, attitude, and atmosphere for every section. Whoever holds all 3 controls the station. Junction 2 sits 40 meters from the jump-sail capacitor bank. There, station rules forbid any weapon heavier than a needle pistol, and that rule is strict for good reason. A single hit on the capacitor bank would permanently destroy the station's ability to recharge ships, for everyone.

The deeper problem is commercial. The mail circuit stops here because the anchorage is neutral, legally bonded, and uneventful. The 5 courier captains have told both sides plainly: fire one shot aboard the station, by anyone against anyone, and the circuit moves to a rival hub. That reroute costs them 11 extra days, but they will take it to stay safe. So the station is only worth owning if the fight over it never turns violent. This warning is a joint letter from the captains, 12 days old, and it is reliable.

objectives.primary: Keep the anchorage running under your employer through the quarterly convergence. No shot may be fired aboard the station.
objectives.secondary: Settle who owns the station in a way the courier captains accept as fair. That means verification, arbitration, or a signed surrender of the claim.
objectives.bonus: Get the convergence done on time. All 5 courier ships dock, swap cargo, and leave inside their 60-hour window, with no mail seized or searched by either side.

complications.name: The Deeds Cannot Be Verified
complications.text: The only registry that can confirm whether Meridian's deeds are genuine is behind the Fortress wall. The nearest working archive that holds Combine records is 2 jumps away — {ARCHIVE_ROUND_TRIP} days for a round trip by hired berth.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until verification finishes, no action can treat the deeds as proven true or false. Say the unit acts early and backs the wrong side. When the truth comes out later, the unit pays the full legal and reputation cost for that mistake.

complications.name: Custody Taken One Step at a Time
complications.text: Meridian never escalates by more than a single guard post, junction, or 'safety inspection' at a time. Each step is too small to be worth fighting over — but the steps add up to control of the whole station.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every 4 to 6 days, Meridian takes one small custody action. Each one the unit lets pass moves real control a step toward Meridian. Undoing a step by force is the first act of violence, and both sides are waiting to pin that on the other.

complications.name: The Capacitor No-Fire Rule
complications.text: Within 60 meters of the sail capacitor bank, station rules allow no weapon heavier than a needle pistol — a rule both sides obey, because firing anything heavier could destroy the very station they are fighting to own.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Inside the Junction 2 zone, combat is limited to needler, melee, and grappling regardless of what either side carries elsewhere. Any energy or ballistic weapon fired in the zone rolls for capacitor damage; a capacitor hit permanently destroys the station's ability to recharge ships.

decisionPoints.name: Settling Who Owns the Station
decisionPoints.context: The deeds are either genuine or a well-made forgery, and finding out takes {ARCHIVE_ROUND_TRIP} days at best. Meridian's next personnel rotation arrives in 23 days and will double the number of guards they have aboard.

options.title: Send to the Archive for a Ruling
advantages: The only path that produces a real answer about the deeds
A signed hold-in-place deal freezes joint custody while you wait. Meridian signs it, because waiting suits their incoming guards
The courier captains respect the proper process, and they say so on the circuit
disadvantages: You share control for {ARCHIVE_ROUND_TRIP} days with a rival who takes ground one step at a time
The archive may hold no answer at all. Its Combine records stop 6 years ago
The hold-in-place deal makes every step Meridian has already taken look legal
options.consequence: An answer comes back in 5 to 8 weeks. It lands into whatever control each side holds by then. You are betting the paperwork arrives before Meridian quietly takes the rest of the station, and that your archive run beats their reinforcement ship.

costs.resource: one courier round trip ({ARCHIVE_ROUND_TRIP} days) of shared custody, with Meridian's guard count doubling on day 23
costs.risk: the archive most likely returns no records at all. The question stays open, and you have given up half the station while waiting for that non-answer.

options.title: Convene the Captains' Board
advantages: Arbitration by the 5 mail captains: fast — convened and decided within 12 days
Their verdict carries the only enforcement that matters out here: the circuit will stop wherever the board names as the lawful operator
Both sides must post good-behavior bonds, which freezes the step-by-step takeover
disadvantages: Neither side is obligated to accept the verdict — only to lose the circuit if they defy it
The captains are not neutral: 2 of the 5 carry cargo for Meridian's parent firm on other routes
A ruling against the employer ends the unit's contract — through an arbitration the unit itself proposed
options.consequence: The captains who need the station calm decide its fate within 12 days. But you have staked your employer's claim on judges you cannot pick, and two of them have ties to the other side.

costs.resource: an arbitration bond lodged with the board, forfeit if the unit's side takes any custody step during the proceedings
costs.risk: 2 of the 5 judges carry the rival's parent-firm cargo elsewhere — a conflict of interest that is known, disclosed, and impossible to remove

options.title: Expel Meridian Before Their Reinforcements Arrive
advantages: Decisive while the numbers still favor the unit: {MERIDIAN_GUARDS} guards now, versus double after day 23
Crowd-control guards are not boarding troops — a planned, bloodless push back to their DropShip is achievable
Restores sole control of the station before the convergence window
disadvantages: If the deeds later prove genuine, the unit has committed armed seizure of a lawful owner's property — piracy, in the only courts left
A bloodless expulsion requires Meridian to also choose bloodless
The captains' letter does not care who shoots first; it counts any shot fired at all
options.consequence: Within 72 hours the station is whole again, or it is a battlefield with a capacitor bank in the middle of it. Either way, you have not settled who owns the deeds. That question still waits for a court to rule on it.

costs.resource: the unit's legal standing, staked entirely on deeds it has not seen proven false
costs.risk: one weapon fired near Junction 2 and the prize both sides are fighting for ceases to exist

decisionPoints.name: Where to Position for a Fight
decisionPoints.context: If it does come to a fight despite everything, the station's layout will decide it, and that layout was fixed years ago by whoever built the Spine. So pick your ground now. Once a fight starts, there is no time left to choose it.

options.title: Hold the Dock Ring
advantages: Keeps any fight 700 meters away from the capacitors
Controls every arrival, departure, and resupply — including Meridian's reinforcement ship
Defensible with a single platoon; the bulkheads favor whoever is dug in
disadvantages: Gives up the 3 valve junctions, and with them control of power and atmosphere scheduling
Whoever controls life support controls the negotiation
options.consequence: The unit controls the doors and Meridian controls the air. The station settles into a standoff where each side withholds utilities or access from the other — stable right up until the convergence makes the doors worth fighting for.

costs.resource: the valve junctions: power and atmosphere scheduling handed to the rival's control
costs.risk: negotiating from the doorway against an opponent who controls the heat and air

options.title: Hold the Three Junctions
advantages: Whoever holds all 3 junctions runs the station in practice, whatever the deeds say
Setting the air and power schedule gives you legal, on-the-record pressure you can also reverse
disadvantages: Junction 2 sits inside the capacitor zone, so the post that matters most is one where your own heavy weapons are banned
Stretches the detail thin across 800 meters of corridor, with Meridian's people posted between your posts
options.consequence: You control the station, but the key post is Junction 2, and it can only be held with needle pistols. That is the one place where a single mistake cannot be undone. It is the post you can least afford to lose and the hardest one to defend.

costs.resource: a continuous 3-post garrison across 800 meters — the detail's entire reserve, tied down as fixed posts
costs.risk: the decisive position sits inside the zone where one ballistic round destroys the station

options.title: Wage an Administrative Siege
advantages: No change in posture at all: the stationmaster reschedules power, water, and galley priority by the book, section by section, against Meridian's quarters
Every measure is documented, lawful, and individually trivial — Meridian's own one-step-at-a-time method turned back on them
To escalate, Meridian has to be the side that visibly breaks station law
disadvantages: Slow: weeks to have an effect, and the reinforcement ship arrives in the meantime
Invites the same treatment in return from whichever junctions Meridian holds
The captains will see a cold, dark guest section at convergence and draw their own conclusions about how 'uneventful' the station still is
options.consequence: The standoff becomes a slow contest of who can make the other more uncomfortable. Each side cuts the other's comforts strictly by the rulebook and waits for the other to slip. Meanwhile the convergence closes in on a station that is quietly turning miserable.

costs.resource: the station's reputation for uneventful neutrality, spent one cold shower at a time in front of the mail circuit
costs.risk: each small measure answered with another — the exact step-by-step escalation the rival started, now run by both sides at once

entries.event: Alarm: Meridian detail moves on Spine Junction 2 during the 0400 watch turnover — 12 personnel, restraint kit, a locksmith, and a notary with a camera.
Unit reaction element reaches Junction 1; Meridian locksmith begins work on the Junction 2 valve council lockout.
Stationmaster declares an ordinance violation over the all-station ring; both legal teams begin recording.
Meridian site director offers a 'joint operations protocol' for Junction 2 — signature in exchange for withdrawal, deadline one hour.
Offer lapses. Whoever physically controls Junction 2 at this mark controls atmosphere scheduling for the dock ring through the convergence.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The quarterly convergence opens in {CONVERGENCE_DAY} days and runs 60 hours. Whoever runs the anchorage that week runs the mail of 5 systems, and their version of this standoff is the one everyone hears. Fire one shot before or during the convergence, by anyone against anyone, and the circuit moves to the rival hub for good. You do not lose the station by running out of time. You lose it the moment someone opens fire.

opforSketch.composition: Meridian Custodial Group site element: {MERIDIAN_GUARDS} licensed security personnel (Green as soldiers, Veteran as process-servers) — riot kit, restraint tools, needlers, body cameras, 2 corporate counsel, and a site director with settlement authority. After day 23: double headcount plus a 6-person 'technical assessment team' whose kit manifests do not parse as crowd control. No 'Mechs, no battle armor; the battlefield is corridors, ledgers, and cameras.
opforSketch.behavior: Advances one small step at a time by design: never the first to escalate visibly, always taking the next step right after the unit takes one. Films everything, litigates everything, and treats every reaction the unit makes as evidence for a future legal filing. Will back down from any single confrontation rather than open fire — and will be back 6 days later, one step further along.

forks.name: OPERATION BONDED RING
forks.trigger: The convergence finishes on time under your employer's control, and the ownership question is either settled or formally filed for a ruling.
forks.consequence: The captains' board makes the anchorage a neutral bonded port, backed by the circuit, with your unit as its standing security on a multi-year retainer. It is the quiet, permanent contract every merc outfit says it wants, until it actually has one.

forks.name: OPERATION DEAD FILE
forks.trigger: Control of the station is lost, or the deeds win at the captains' board, or the circuit reroutes.
forks.consequence: The ousted stationmaster still holds the Combine's original ownership records, the only papers that can reopen the case. Meridian's parent firm has hired fast transport to chase him down. The follow-on is a 2-jump race to the archive, with a clerk's strongbox of records as the prize.

forks.name: OPERATION JURY RIG
forks.trigger: Any exchange of fire aboard, or any capacitor damage, no matter who fired.
forks.consequence: The circuit reroutes and the station's trade dies within a week. The stranded mail, 5 systems' worth of bonded cargo and letters, sits in a crippled station that every opportunist within 2 jumps has now heard about. Your unit is left guarding a broken waystation full of other people's mail.

storyElementSeed: Third watch in the Spine. A guard from each company stands 40 meters apart under the capacitor warning signs. Neither is allowed a real weapon. They share the silence, and eventually a thermos that neither one will report.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Send to the Archive for a Ruling
resourceGates.lackingText: No owned JumpShip: the query rides a hired berth on a mail captain's schedule — add 9,000 C-bills and up to 14 days, and the captain carrying the question is also a potential juror.
Option renders locked: ARBITRATION BOND REQUIRED — the board seats nobody who cannot post forfeit money, and a letter of credit drawn on a bank nobody can reach does not count.

title: OPERATION SILENT LOOM
skeleton: security force must keep a covert factory conversion secret for a fixed build time while every measure that protects the site advertises it, and the decisive question is which day the asset stops being worth abandoning
inspiration: Weimar Germany's clandestine rearmament — hidden production lines and the black Reichswehr, 1922-33
situation:
{WORLD}, 3134. The {TARGET_FACTION}'s presence here is a Standing Guard company at the spaceport, 90 kilometers from the valley, led by officers who have not been paid from the capital in 2 years and know it. The {EMPLOYER}'s presence is quieter. Plant 4 of the {WORLD} Agricultural Combine, called 'the Loom' by its workers, is {BUILD_DAYS} days from finishing a secret conversion. It is being retooled from building AgroMech farm 'Mechs to building BattleMechs. The machine tools arrived over 7 months in crates labeled as irrigation equipment. Your unit holds the security contract under a cover name: 'Combine Industrial Safety Division,' reporting to {NPC:employer-contact}, whose own line of authority is something one learns not to ask about.

This contract is the reverse of a normal garrison job. Here, being discovered is worse than being destroyed. A burned factory is just a tragedy. A discovered weapons plant is a provocation. If the plant surfaces now, the production line is only half-built and cannot defend itself. The Standing Guard would be obligated to act, and the pro-{TARGET_FACTION} Citizens' Committee would hand them the reason to do it. So every normal security measure actually gives the secret away. A new fence signals there is something new to hide. A patrol pattern traces the perimeter for anyone watching. A single sweep of air-search radar would be picked up from the spaceport tower within the hour.

The key terrain problem is the terrace locks. Plant 4 sits among the valley's terraced fields. The only heavy-truck route in crosses the lock stair: 4 water locks that can be heard from 2 kilometers away and seen from the public highway. Lock-keepers run them, and their families have logged every lock cycle in ledger books for 5 generations. Moving convoys at night does not hide them. It just creates a record of unexplained night traffic. Right now the keepers' ledgers show {LOCK_CYCLES} unexplained night cycles over the past 60 days, and the Citizens' Committee has started asking to borrow those books. This comes from committee minutes 9 days old, and it is reliable.

One leak is already active. A shipping clerk inside Plant 4 has been photographing truck paperwork. {NPC:intel-source} has identified the clerk, but not who is receiving the photos. They travel by hand, at bicycle speed, to a new drop point every fourth day. On {WORLD} this year, no one can chase a courier that slow and still catch him. But you can outpace him with a single decision made now.

objectives.primary: Get the Loom to production day without the Standing Guard finding it and without the Citizens' Committee being able to prove it. That means {BUILD_DAYS} days of secrecy, bought without adding visible security.
objectives.secondary: Contain the paperwork leak. Find who is receiving the photos and shut that channel down, take it over, or feed it lies. Do it without a disappearance the valley would notice.
objectives.bonus: Reach production day with the lock-keepers' ledgers handled first. Borrow them, copy them, buy them, or make the entries look boring, before the Committee reads them.

complications.name: Protecting the Site Exposes It
complications.text: Fences, patrols, lights, radar — each one protects the plant and advertises it at the same time. The first rule of this contract is to add as little visible security as possible.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every visible security measure the unit adds raises the site's discovery index. No single event triggers exposure. It is the rising index that decides when the Standing Guard's curiosity becomes a real inspection, and when the Committee's suspicion becomes a printed accusation.

complications.name: The Lock-Keepers' Ledgers
complications.text: Five generations of lock-cycle logs, kept in pencil, accurate to the minute, sitting in 4 lockhouses along the public highway. The best surveillance network on {WORLD} was built by the canal authority in 3071 and never meant to be one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every heavy shipment to Plant 4 creates a permanent ledger entry. Scheduling convoys can shape how the entries look, but it cannot erase them. The ledgers act as a discovery clock that only counts up. It keeps rising unless the unit deals with it at the decision point or through complication play.

complications.name: The Unpaid Garrison
complications.text: The Standing Guard company is professional, bored, broke, and 90 kilometers away. No one has given them anything worth dying for in a long time. What they would do if they discovered the plant is genuinely unknown — enforce the law, demand a bribe, sell the secret, or all three one after another.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On any discovery event, roll the Standing Guard's reaction (enforce the law / demand a bribe to stay quiet / sell the secret to the Committee / sell it to the {EMPLOYER}), weighted by the player's prior dealings with the garrison. They may act as an enemy, as a seller to be bought, or as both.

decisionPoints.name: Handling the Manifest Leak
decisionPoints.context: The clerk photographs the truck paperwork, and the photos travel by bicycle to an unknown reader every fourth day. The clerk's supervisor is owed money; the clerk's sister teaches the lock-keepers' children. On a world this small, everyone is connected to everyone.

options.title: Arrest the Clerk Quietly
advantages: The leak stops completely on the day of the arrest
Interrogation may identify who was receiving the photos before they notice the photos have stopped
disadvantages: On a world this small, a person vanishing is more conspicuous than the plant being discovered — the valley notices a missing neighbor faster than the Committee reads ledgers
If the recipient is the Standing Guard, the leak suddenly going dark tells them they were spotted — which tells them there was something worth spotting
options.consequence: Silence, bought at the cost of being noticed. The leak stops and the question of who was reading it goes unanswered — unless the reader, noticing the sudden quiet, decides to come and look in person.

costs.resource: the valley's lack of attention: one person's disappearance, noticed by a town that keeps track of everyone
costs.risk: shutting down the leak is itself a message to whoever was receiving it

options.title: Feed the Leak False Information
advantages: The leak becomes a tool: rewrite the paperwork to show irrigation equipment, farm tooling, nothing of interest
The recipient's reactions to specific planted items will eventually reveal who they are
Nothing visible changes, so the discovery index stays flat
disadvantages: Requires 30 days of flawless document forgery inside a working plant
If the clerk or the reader catches the substitution, every previous month of real paperwork is confirmed as having been worth photographing
options.consequence: The plant runs a second, fake production line on paper, for a reader whose reach you do not know. Done perfectly, it buys the entire build window. Done wrong, a single mismatched serial number confirms the plant's real secret.

costs.resource: 30 days of flawless forgery: a documents team working without a single error inside a live plant
costs.risk: one detected forgery turns the deception into confirmation, and worse than if the leak had simply been left alone

options.title: Accelerate the Build
advantages: Cut the schedule from {BUILD_DAYS} days toward 100 by adding day shifts — the race simply ends sooner
Every day cut is a day the leak, the ledgers, and the garrison matter less
Once the line passes the point where it can defend itself, discovery stops being fatal and becomes merely a diplomatic problem
disadvantages: Day shifts triple the workforce's exposure: more new hires, more traffic, more lock cycles in the ledgers
Discovery becomes near-certain around day 120 of the compressed schedule — the bet is that the line can defend itself before then
options.consequence: You spend secrecy to buy speed, and once the line is finished, it cannot be undone. The question is no longer whether {WORLD} finds out. It is what day they find out, and what is standing in Bay 3, ready to fight, that morning.

costs.resource: the secret itself, spent gradually: the discovery index rises every week of the compressed schedule
costs.risk: the projection puts discovery around day 120 against the line being defensible around day 100 — a 20-day safety margin built entirely from estimates

decisionPoints.name: Handling the Inspection Notice
decisionPoints.context: The Standing Guard announces a routine industrial-safety inspection of Combine facilities {INSPECTION_NOTICE} days from now — Plant 4 is fourth on the list. The letter calls it routine. By now, nobody on either side believes anything is routine.

options.title: Disguise the Plant
advantages: A 40-day partial teardown restores Buildings 1-3 to convincing farm-'Mech production; the new weapons line is compressed into Building 4 behind a certified hazardous-materials wall
Passes a genuine routine inspection completely
disadvantages: Costs 40 days off the build schedule, spent whether or not the inspection was ever a real threat
If the inspectors were tipped off — by the leak's reader or by the ledgers — the disguise work is exactly what they will photograph as evidence
options.consequence: The weapons line stays hidden, protected by the delay itself. But the schedule now slips into the season when the Committee starts reading the ledgers. And the question of who tipped off the inspectors stays open, sitting behind a freshly painted hazard wall.

costs.resource: the build schedule: 40 days spent on disguise instead of production
costs.risk: the disguise defeats a routine inspection but is incriminating evidence under a tipped-off one — and the unit cannot tell which kind is coming

options.title: Bribe the Inspector
advantages: The garrison is 2 years unpaid; the prefecture official who writes the inspection findings has a price {NPC:intel-source} can estimate to within 10 percent
The inspection happens, the report says irrigation plant, and the build never stops
disadvantages: A bribed officer stays bribed only until someone offers more — and the bribe creates the first hard evidence of {EMPLOYER} involvement, where none existed before
It reverses the whole point of deniability: the cover story now comes with a paper trail
options.consequence: The cheapest option in days and the most expensive in the long run. The Loom's secret now has a second owner in a {TARGET_FACTION} uniform, and the danger from him grows the more nervous he gets.

costs.resource: deniability: the operation's first hard evidence, held by a man in the enemy's uniform
costs.risk: every bribed official is a future blackmail or auction risk — his price could be estimated precisely because his loyalty is for sale

options.title: Stage a Hazard Lockout
advantages: A staged chemical-release incident seals Building 4 under the Combine's own certified hazard rules — the inspectors legally cannot enter
Buildings 1-3 inspect clean and genuinely; the inspection passes on its own paperwork
disadvantages: Hazard rules require a follow-up safety review in 60 days — so the inspection problem is not cancelled, just postponed
A second hazard lockout timed to that follow-up review will not look like an accident to anyone
options.consequence: The inspection is defeated using its own rulebook, but the price is a new and harder deadline. The Loom must be finished, defensible, or emptied within 60 days — because the next inspection arrives with the legal right to enter.

costs.resource: the hazard rules: a one-time legal shield, now spent, with a mandatory 60-day return inspection attached
costs.risk: the staged accident must also convince the Combine's own safety office — people who know exactly what the plant really builds

entries.event: Discovery alarm: Standing Guard duty officer receives actionable evidence of the Plant 4 line — source per discovery event (ledgers, leak, inspection, or emission).
Garrison commander gathers his officers and decides how to respond: enforce the law, extort a bribe, or sell the secret. Landline traffic from the DropPort spikes.
Citizens' Committee learns independently or by garrison leak; printing presses in the valley town begin a broadsheet run.
If the garrison chose to enforce, a Standing Guard column forms for the 90 km road march: 8 to 11 vehicles and 1 'Mech lance.
Column reaches the lock stair: single-file crossing, 90 minutes, the only approach wide enough for armor.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The line becomes defensible on day {DEFENSE_DAY} of the build. Before that day, the right answer to discovery is to destroy your own work and evacuate the 60 technicians. After that day, the line can build 'Mechs to defend itself. So every decision here is a bet on which side of day {DEFENSE_DAY} the alarm sounds. When it does sound, it starts an 18-hour clock, and that clock ends at a lock stair a single lance can hold or lose.

opforSketch.composition: Standing Guard company: 1 BattleMech lance (aging {TARGET_FACTION} models, Regular), 2 motorized infantry platoons, 8-11 light vehicles — professional, unpaid, and unpredictable in allegiance. Citizens' Committee: no combat value; its weapon is publication and the garrison's obligation to respond. Generator should treat the garrison's posture roll as the seed's true OPFOR variable: the same column arrives as law, as extortion, or as a rival bidder.
opforSketch.behavior: The Standing Guard fights like a garrison defending its own reason to exist: by the book, tied to the roads, and committed only when it has a documented justification. If its reaction is to extort or to sell, contact opens as a negotiation conducted from firing positions rather than a battle. The Committee escalates through publication: every accusation it prints forces someone to act, usually someone other than the Committee.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRST THREAD
forks.trigger: The Loom reaches production day undiscovered, or after it passes day {DEFENSE_DAY} and can defend itself.
forks.consequence: The first batch of finished 'Mechs must move. 6 machines, by night, down the same lock stair the ledgers record, to a DropShip whose manifest says farm equipment. It is the same secrecy problem as before, but now each machine weighs 75 tons more, and the {TARGET_FACTION} will not move the deadline.

forks.name: OPERATION TORN CLOTH
forks.trigger: The plant is discovered before day {DEFENSE_DAY}, with the Standing Guard choosing to enforce the law.
forks.consequence: The unit must destroy its own half-built line and get 60 technicians off {WORLD}, through a spaceport the Standing Guard controls. Each of those technicians could rebuild the line somewhere else, so both the {TARGET_FACTION} remnant and the Committee now want to identify every one of them.

forks.name: OPERATION EVEN HAND
forks.trigger: The Committee publishes its analysis of the ledgers without the garrison acting — an accusation with no proof behind it.
forks.consequence: The valley town splits over what is really in Building 4, with crowds marching on the Combine gates and the Standing Guard refusing to take either side. The unit has to hold the plant's perimeter against crowds it cannot fire on, under a cover name that says Industrial Safety.

storyElementSeed: Dusk at the third lock. The keeper's daughter does her arithmetic homework against the ledger stand while the gates fill, and writes the truck count in the margin the way her father taught her: without being asked, without looking up.

is-liao.objectives.primary: The Loom must finish its work unseen. That means {BUILD_DAYS} days of perfect secrecy. The Chancellor's gift to {WORLD} is delivered whole, or it is not delivered at all. A half-built plant that is discovered does not count as partial success. It is a failure, and worse than never having begun.

resourceGates.lackingText: Option locked: COMBINE CO-FUNDING REQUIRED. Triple shifts must be paid in cash that the cover-name payroll cannot account for. Without that cash reserve, the acceleration is just a memo and cannot happen.

No secure documents team: the forgery work has to run out of a rented print shop in the valley town — add 4,000 C-bills per month, and one more civilian landlord who must never start to wonder what the unit is doing.

title: OPERATION HEARTH WOLF
skeleton: hunter must carve a raider band out of the population that raised it, where every settlement's testimony is a weapon in its feud with the next settlement over, and checking any lead in person costs the days that let the band dissolve back into the crowd
inspiration: sub-Roman Britain after the legions — endemic warbands living inside the communities they tax, 5th century
situation:
The {WORLD} steppe never had an HPG worth missing, but the Blackout hurt it anyway. When the trading networks died in 3134, the off-world grain buyers stopped coming and the cash economy left with them. What filled the gap is what the Landholders' Moot calls banditry. Half the steppe just calls it normal life. The band uses no name for itself. The Moot's contract calls them the Hearth Wolves. Collected testimony puts the band at {BAND_FIGHTERS} fighters, 5-7 armed vehicles, and 1 working BattleMech: a Rifleman with a dead left arm. Eleven witnesses across 4 raids confirm the Rifleman, so treat that as solid. The rest of the counts are 20 to 90 days old and shakier, so treat them as a rough guide, not a hard number.

The Wolves never leave the planet, because they have nowhere to go and no reason to. They live inside the steppe's 9 settlements as sons, cousins, and in-laws. They raid overland between harvests, and the stolen goods flow back home as favors: a grain store refilled here, a water pump fixed there, a wedding paid for. Every settlement swears the Wolves are based in the next settlement over. But each such accusation is also a weapon in some old water-rights feud, grazing dispute, or marriage grudge. Your employer is the Moot itself: {EMPLOYER}, working through {NPC:employer-contact}. It hired outsiders because no settlement will hunt its own relatives, and no two settlements will hunt together.

The core problem is that the truth costs time. Tips are everywhere and free, but every one has to be checked in person. That runs {LEAD_CHECK_DAYS} days per lead across the steppe's distances. Meanwhile the band needs only about 26 hours of warning to melt back into harvest crews and family homes. So your intelligence budget does not buy facts. It buys claims, sold by people who each have 60 years of reasons to lie.

The key terrain problem is the shelterbelts. These are 200 kilometers of planted windbreak lines, 12 trees deep, that split the steppe into narrow corridors. All vehicle traffic is funneled along them, and any movement throws up a dust plume you can see from 15 kilometers off. The belts also hide anything that holds still inside them. The Wolves grew up reading this ground. You have {CONTRACT_DAYS} days under contract to learn it, and the Moot pays in grain futures, not C-bills. That deadline will not move.

objectives.primary: Stop the organized raiding on the {WORLD} steppe. Break up, capture, or kill the band's fighting core, and take or destroy its Rifleman.
objectives.secondary: Leave the 9 settlements still bound into one community. Do not let your own tip-buying push any feud into open fighting.
objectives.bonus: Map out who fed and sheltered the band, and where the stolen goods went. Hand the Moot a record it can use to settle debts by ruling instead of revenge.

complications.name: Testimony Is a Weapon
complications.text: Every tip is shaped by the informer's own feuds. When you gather intelligence, the settlements use you to hit their rivals. There is no way around it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every lead, whether bought or offered for free, carries a hidden feud-bias rating. If you act on a lead you have not checked, you risk hitting a feud rival instead of the band. Each time that happens, it hands that settlement a fresh grievance and makes all later tips less trustworthy.

complications.name: The 26-Hour Vanishing Act
complications.text: Given about 26 hours of warning, the whole band can turn back into ordinary farmhands. Weapons go under the grain, vehicles into barns, and the Rifleman into one of an estimated 3 prepared hiding spots that nobody has found.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any operation the band learns about more than 26 hours ahead of time finds only civilians when it arrives. After a fight that fails to pin them, the chance of catching the band falls to zero by T+26:00. You can find the Rifleman's hiding spots only through complication play or by seizing the band's favor ledger.

complications.name: Paid in Grain Futures
complications.text: The Moot pays in grain futures that can only be cashed in at harvest. Every day of operations consumes real supplies bought with that paper — and the raids themselves keep driving down what the paper is worth.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The unit operates on a {CONTRACT_DAYS}-day clock with a fixed supply budget. Each major raid the band pulls off reduces the value of the unit's pay by 5-8 percent. Running out of either days or supplies ends the contract, no matter how much progress has been made.

decisionPoints.name: How to Hunt People Who Live Among Their Own
decisionPoints.context: The band cannot be found just by searching. It can only be forced to hold still, lured into the open, or cut off from the supplies that let it stay hidden. Three methods, one budget, and the whole steppe watching to see which one the outsiders choose.

options.title: Run a Vehicle Census
advantages: Registering every vehicle and fuel store, settlement by settlement, chokes off the band's mobility at its source
Methodical, defensible, and produces the first honest baseline data anyone has ever had on the steppe
Relies on no bought testimony at all
disadvantages: Treats the entire population as suspects, in their own homes, for 40 days
The band's vehicles get registered too — by their cousins, as farm equipment, with all the papers in order
Slow enough that the Wolves can simply stop raiding and wait out the contract
options.consequence: The steppe gets mapped, and the steppe remembers being mapped. The band either loses its supply lines or simply waits out the census. Either way, you leave behind one more grievance for the next generation to carry.

costs.resource: the population's patience: 40 days of registration teams in 9 settlements that did not ask for them
costs.risk: a band that has paused looks exactly like a band that has been beaten — until the contract ends and the raids start again

options.title: Buy the Band's Quartermaster
advantages: The Moot's fixer has named the band's supply handler and quoted a price. Turning him buys the favor ledger, the fuel caches, and probably the Rifleman's hiding spots
One deal replaces a whole season of fieldwork
The ledger turns the bonus objective from a hope into a written list
disadvantages: The price includes written amnesty for the handler's entire home settlement, so the other 8 will call the contract bought and the Moot biased
Everything he sells is only his side of the story. Checking any single item still costs {LEAD_CHECK_DAYS} days
If he is playing both sides, you have just paid for the band's counterintelligence
options.consequence: The hunt turns into a business deal, and the deal turns into politics. The ledger is either the key to the whole steppe or a very expensive way to arm one settlement against the rest. You cannot tell which until you have checked each entry in person.

costs.resource: written amnesty for one settlement, paid for with the trust of the other eight
costs.risk: you would be trusting one source for everything. Every entry still needs {LEAD_CHECK_DAYS} days to check, and he knows which ones you will never have time for

options.title: Run a Bait Convoy
advantages: A convoy that looks rich, loaded with salt, medicine, and machine parts, run through the shelterbelt corridors, is the one target the band's favor-trading economy cannot ignore
If they take the bait, the band is caught in the open for the first time in 3 years
Resolved in an afternoon instead of over a season
disadvantages: The band picks which fights to take and may simply let the convoy pass — only 3 runs are budgeted before the supply situation ends the experiment
Convincing bait has to be real cargo, so losing the fight means handing the enemy its best haul in years
The shelterbelts are ambush country for both sides; the trap can be sprung on the unit instead
options.consequence: The whole contract narrows to one engagement in a corridor between windbreaks, on ground both sides chose — with the unit's own supplies riding in the trucks it is using as bait.

costs.resource: the bait cargo: real salt, real medicine, genuinely lost if the fight is lost
costs.risk: 3 budgeted runs against a band that has studied every outsider's habits since the grain buyers stopped coming

decisionPoints.name: The Stolen Grain in the Granaries
decisionPoints.context: A verified lead pays off: a third of last season's stolen grain is sitting in the communal granaries of one settlement — handed out as favors, partly eaten, partly owed against. That settlement's children are being fed on the proceeds of the raid that emptied its rival's grain stores.

options.title: Confiscate It and Return It
advantages: The law as written: stolen goods back to their owners, the Moot's authority enforced in broad daylight
Proves to the victim settlements that the contract actually serves them
Materially weakens the band's standing in its best client settlement
disadvantages: Takes the winter food supply away from one settlement's children to return it to a rival's stores
Turns the band's supporters into the band's recruits within a single season
The convoy out runs 60 kilometers of shelterbelt corridor on a schedule everyone knows
options.consequence: Justice arrives by truck and leaves a settlement hungry. The Moot's law is upheld, the band gains a settlement full of new recruits, and the return convoy is the most exposed target the unit has ever put on a schedule.

costs.resource: the settlement's winter food supply — and with it, the best listening post the unit had into the band's favor network
costs.risk: a 60 km return convoy through ambush corridors, on a published schedule, carrying the band's single strongest recruiting argument

options.title: Record It and Leave It
advantages: The granary becomes a known, watched site on your map. It builds the picture of the band's favor network instead of a list of payback strikes
No settlement starves, and you hand the band no recruiting argument
Costs nothing to carry out
disadvantages: The employer's contract says to recover stolen goods; the victim settlements will eventually learn the unit found their grain and left it there
Once this tolerance is documented, it becomes policy: every other client settlement learns that the worst that happens if you get caught is a note in a ledger
options.consequence: The unit chooses intelligence over returning the grain. The map of the band's favor network grows more complete while the Moot's patience and the victims' trust both run down toward the contract's end date — a race the unit started on purpose.

costs.resource: the victim settlements' trust, spent quietly until the day they learn what you found and ignored
costs.risk: you are choosing to fail one duty on purpose. If the band is not broken before word gets out, that choice is how people will judge the whole contract

options.title: Seal It Under Unit Guard
advantages: The grain stays where the children are, locked under the unit's seal pending a Moot ruling — neither seized back nor abandoned
Forces the Moot to actually build the dispute-resolution process the bonus objective imagines
Makes the unit look like an honest broker to all 9 settlements at once — the first party ever to pull that off
disadvantages: The unit takes over the band's own job. The seal is a promise you now have to guard, and the band's whole standing rests on being the steppe's only protector
The Moot only meets four times a year, so a ruling can take a season, while your contract runs on days
options.consequence: The unit steps into the band's role and beats it at its own game: protection and fairness, with the unit's seal on the granary door. This is the boldest move available. It also makes the band's leaders personal enemies, because it takes away the one thing they truly have, their standing as the steppe's protector.

costs.resource: a permanent guard detail on a granary 60 km from anywhere, for the rest of the contract
costs.risk: you are taking away the band's whole reason to exist. It will strike back at the seal, and it will do it in front of everyone

entries.event: The alarm goes off. The band makes contact: it takes the bait convoy, tests the granary seal, or ambushes a census team. An outrider reports the first shots.
The band's screening vehicles show up in the shelterbelt corridors on both flanks. They keep their dust down and move well. The Rifleman is not in the fight yet.
The band decides whether to stay and fight. They press the attack only if the Rifleman joins in. If it stays hidden, this was just a probe.
Whether they are winning or losing, the band starts breaking off. Its groups peel away down 3 separate corridors.
Dissolution complete: weapons cached, vehicles barned, fighters in harvest crews. Pursuit value zero.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Any single fight is over, for all practical purposes, by T+26:00. After that the band is just 9 settlements of civilians again, and every door you knock on only feeds someone's feud. The bigger clock is your pay. You have {CONTRACT_DAYS} days of grain-future funding, and it loses 5-8 percent of its value with every raid the band pulls off. The Wolves do not have to beat you. They only have to stay hidden until your money runs out.

opforSketch.composition: Endemic raider band: {BAND_FIGHTERS} fighters in squad-scale kin groups (Regular on home ground, Green in any stand-up fight), 5-7 armed agricultural vehicles and technicals, 1 Rifleman with a dead left arm (Veteran pilot, the band's founder). No air, no resupply line — the steppe is the resupply line. Generator should weight engagements toward harassment, screening, and dispersal; the band masses only when the Rifleman commits, which is rare and means the stake is existential to them.
opforSketch.behavior: Refuses battle by default; fights only on shelterbelt ground of its own choosing, and only to protect its favor network or the Rifleman. It prefers to tax rather than destroy, to shame rather than kill, and to scatter on its 26-hour clock rather than take casualties. Its counterintelligence is the steppe itself: every settlement contains its informers, including the settlements it raids.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET HARVEST
forks.trigger: The band's core is broken or has surrendered, with the Rifleman accounted for.
forks.consequence: The Moot asks the unit to stand guarantee over the season of amnesty and payback that follows.
