You garrison the steppe as a neutral force for one harvest, while the debts from the favor network are settled by ruling. It is the rare contract where no one shoots, unless someone does.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND WOLF
forks.trigger: The contract expires with the band still intact, or a mistaken strike on a feud rival destroys the Moot's authority.
forks.consequence: The grievances your hunt created unite the steppe's young men faster than the Wolves ever could. The new band is twice the size, and off-world fences now arrive by tramp freighter to buy its loot. The Moot's next contract pays even less, because the harvest it is drawn against is worth less than before.

forks.name: OPERATION DEN DIGGING
forks.trigger: The band's fighting core is broken but the Rifleman and the leadership escape the steppe.
forks.consequence: The band's founder flees into the karst country beyond the shelterbelts, real badlands with 1 prepared fallback camp marked in the quartermaster's ledger. The passes close with the first snows in 30-40 days. The follow-on is a raid on that fixed camp, racing a weather deadline.

storyElementSeed: A granary office, evening. The unit's quartermaster counts sacks against a ledger while a settlement elder watches, and both of them pretend not to recognize the third handwriting in the margins — the band keeps better books than the Moot.

resourceGates.lackingText: You have no depot under contract, so the bait cargo has to be bought at the steppe's scarcity prices. Add 11,000 C-bills. Worse, the buying itself tells every fixer on the steppe that a rich convoy is coming.
Option locked: you need hard currency. The handler will not sell for grain futures, for the same reason no one else on the steppe will take them.

title: OPERATION TWO BANNERS
skeleton: instructor must run one school for two rival student formations who will jointly inherit the planet's only arsenal, while every grade, crew assignment, and range day is read by both sponsors as a ruling on who owns the world
inspiration: Whampoa Military Academy — Nationalist and Communist cadets under one commandant, 1924-26
situation:
{WORLD}, 3136. The Republic's local government here collapsed quietly, and what replaced it is a simple, dangerous problem of numbers. The {EMPLOYER}'s civil-affairs mission sponsors a Self-Defense Cooperative of 130 trainees, paid in {EMPLOYER} scrip. Its liaison officer's loyalty to the {EMPLOYER} is the planet's worst-kept secret. The old Republic-chartered Militia Association still musters 110. The planetary assembly has to defend a world both groups claim to love. It has signed one training contract, yours, with three signatures on it: the Cooperative, the Association, and the assembly itself. One school. One curriculum. Two banners over the parade ground, by agreement, at exactly equal height.

The real problem is the inheritance. {WORLD}'s entire arsenal is just {MACHINES} working machines in the school's motor pool: 3 BattleMechs (a Panther, a Spider, and a Blackjack) and 5 armed IndustrialMech conversions. Under Article 9 of the contract, the whole arsenal passes at graduation to 'the certified planetary defense formation,' meaning one single formation. The people who wrote the contract could not agree which group that would be, so they funded the school and put off the fight. As a result, every grade, crew slot, and demerit your instructors hand out is read two ways: as training, and as a ruling on who will own the planet. Both sponsors keep score sheets. You have seen the Cooperative's, which is only 6 days old, so treat it as current. Assume the Association keeps one too.

The key terrain problem is the firing range. The only live-fire ground on {WORLD} is a stretch of salt flats. You share it with {WORLD}'s civilian harvest crews on a fixed schedule the assembly will not change, because the salt harvest is what pays for the school. The whole course allows only 12 live-fire days, and weather has already cancelled 3. Deciding which platoons get the remaining {RANGE_DAYS} is itself a ruling on who matters more, and everyone is keeping count.

There is no higher authority to appeal to. The {EMPLOYER}'s district command answers in one courier round trip at best. The Republic never answers at all, and the assembly answers only in committee. So whatever standards this school sets, the only thing that will hold them up on {WORLD} is people's habit of respecting them. You have {SYLLABUS_DAYS} days to build that habit in 240 people who are already, quietly, two opposing armies.

objectives.primary: Graduate one certified formation under Article 9. It can be integrated, run in parallel, or built some other way. Just make sure no one seizes the arsenal by force before, during, or at the ceremony.
objectives.secondary: Certify crews for all {MACHINES} machines to a trained standard or better. Leave the motor pool with upkeep habits it can keep going after you are gone.
objectives.bonus: Get all three signers to agree, in writing, on what Article 9 actually means before graduation day. This is the very question the drafters ducked.

complications.name: The Score Sheets
complications.text: Both sponsors track every grade, crew slot, and demerit by which faction it lands on. A failed inspection looks like deliberate sabotage. An honest commendation looks like favoritism. To be believed at all, the school has to look perfectly even-handed to everyone watching.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track how fair the school looks, as a separate score from how good its training actually is. Any decision that tips that fairness score toward one side can trigger sponsor protests, suspended stipends, or trainee walkouts. This happens even when the decision was the right call on training merit.

complications.name: Twelve Days of Live Fire
complications.text: Live-fire on the saltpan only happens when the schedule allows it and the weather cooperates. Three days are already gone. There is exactly enough BattleMech ammunition for the planned curriculum plus one emergency reserve, and no more.
complications.mechanicalEffect: {RANGE_DAYS} range days remain, and each day covers 2 platoons. The schedule is a public document. Roll for weather cancellation on each scheduled day. Cancelled days cannot be made up, and the platoons that lost them treat it as a grievance.

complications.name: The Liaison Is Watching
complications.text: The {EMPLOYER} liaison observes everything and writes a great deal down. His reports travel by courier, his suggestions are phrased as polite requests, and the unit has no way to know how much patience he has left.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The liaison, {NPC:opfor-commander}, is the standing antagonist here, not an enemy on the field. He keeps offering 'observations' that are really tests. How you respond shifts the {EMPLOYER} sponsor's behavior and sets how bad the day-{ALARM_DAY} event will be.

decisionPoints.name: Designing the Command Structure
decisionPoints.context: Article 9 demands one formation. The curriculum has to produce a command structure, and that command structure is who inherits the arsenal. The unit decides how to build it before the sponsors settle the question by force.

options.title: Strict Merit, One Combined List
advantages: Honest, defensible, and the only standard a professional school can certify under its own name
Produces the best command structure the trainee pool can actually support
Neither sponsor can claim the ranking was bought — only that it was wrong
disadvantages: The list will be mixed between the two factions, and a mixed chain of command pleases neither sponsor's score sheet
Both sponsors have already drafted their sabotage accusations in advance, ready for whenever their candidates rank low
options.consequence: The school bets everything on the standard itself. If the standard holds, {WORLD} gets a real formation. If either sponsor rejects the list, the school has certified a formation that exists only on paper. Under Article 9, that paper formation now owns every machine on the planet.

costs.resource: the school's neutrality: spent on a single published list, with no chance for a second version
costs.risk: a rejected merit list leaves the entire arsenal legally deeded to a formation that fell apart in the assembly hall

options.title: Two Parallel Companies, Split Arsenal
advantages: Realistic: train two companies under their own banners, split the machines 4 and 4, and certify both
Each sponsor disciplines its own people, which halves the school's discipline problem
Graduation day arrives with no winner-take-all decision in it
disadvantages: Breaks the plain words of Article 9, which call for one formation, not two, and puts your name on the violation
Arms both factions equally and makes splitting the planet a graduation requirement
The 'Mechs cannot actually be split evenly. One machine is left over, and it is a war waiting to start over who gets it
options.consequence: The school answers the political question by formalizing the split. {WORLD} gets two small armies with diplomas, and the unit's signature is on the partition. The peace lasts exactly as long as the two sides stay evenly matched.

costs.resource: Article 9 itself, broken by the very people running the school, with the assembly's lawyers watching
costs.risk: {MACHINES} does not split evenly in two, so one machine is left over, and that leftover becomes the most dangerous object on the planet

options.title: Deliberately Mixed Crews
advantages: Every multi-crew machine gets a mixed crew on purpose. Every BattleMech pilot gets a wingman and a technician from the other faction, so neither faction can field the arsenal without the other
Builds the two sides' need for each other right into how the formation fights
Quietly serves the {EMPLOYER}'s goal, because the design teaches integration that no lecture could
disadvantages: Slow: mixed crews perform worse for 30-40 days before they perform at all, and the limited range days pay that cost
A single publicized fistfight in one crew bay could discredit the whole approach
Both sponsors will recognize the design for what it is — a trap built from their mutual dependence
options.consequence: The school builds the integration into the machines themselves, so that rejecting it costs the rejecter the use of the arsenal. It is the most durable answer and the most fragile to execute: the design cannot be announced, only revealed gradually as the crews graduate working together.

costs.resource: {RANGE_DAYS} range days spent on crews that shoot worse before they shoot better
costs.risk: the design only works if it is discovered slowly — announced or exposed early, it looks like sabotage aimed at both sponsors at once

decisionPoints.name: The Liaison's Dossier
decisionPoints.context: On day {ALARM_DAY}, the {EMPLOYER} liaison hands you documents showing that 6 Association trainees plan to seize the motor pool on the eve of graduation. The documents are convincing. But the source is one of the two factions, and there is no way to check the papers independently on {WORLD}. The nearest neutral judge is a full courier round trip away.

options.title: Expel the Six Trainees
advantages: If the dossier is true, the plot dies when the six are removed from the rolls
Shows the school enforces security regardless of which faction is involved
The liaison's sponsor is satisfied, and the stipend money keeps flowing
disadvantages: Acting on one faction's evidence against the other's trainees ends the school's neutrality with a single order
If the dossier was faked, the unit has just done the {EMPLOYER}'s work of removing the Association's best cadets — exactly as the fake was designed to make it do
options.consequence: Six trainees are gone, and the school has shown whose side it takes when it reads a document. True or false, the dossier did its job. The only open question is whose job that was.

costs.resource: the school's neutrality, traded away for one faction's evidence file
costs.risk: if the dossier was faked, then expelling the six is the real sabotage, and you carried it out under the school's own signature

options.title: Lock the Arsenal and Delay the Handover
advantages: The motor pool goes under unit guard with a dual-key lock. Graduation still happens, but the Article 9 transfer waits until the dossier can be checked
Punishes no one on the strength of unverified paperwork
A neutral judge from a neighboring circuit can rule on the dossier, one courier round trip, or {COURIER_JUDGE} days
disadvantages: Both sponsors read the lockout as the unit seizing the arsenal for itself — the one thing they will agree on
{COURIER_JUDGE} days of armed standoff with two certified formations and zero machines handed over
The contract's payments are tied to the handover the unit just postponed
options.consequence: The unit becomes the planet's arsenal-keeper to avoid becoming its judge. A verdict arrives at courier speed into a parade-ground standoff that worsens with time — but no one was expelled on faith, and the school keeps its integrity.

costs.resource: one courier round trip ({COURIER_JUDGE} days) of locked-down standoff, with the handover payment frozen alongside it
costs.risk: the only thing both sides on {WORLD} agree on becomes that the foreign school stole the arsenal under cover of paperwork

options.title: Read the Dossier Aloud to Everyone
advantages: Brief both sponsors and the assembly together. Lay out the dossier, its source, and the fact that it cannot be verified, and let full openness be the only fair option left
Forces the liaison to either stand behind his document in public or disown it
If the plot is real, the plotters now know they are exposed, so the graduation-eve risk likely fades on its own
disadvantages: Panics everyone at once: graduation week proceeds under open mutual suspicion and doubled guard rosters
The liaison's sponsor treats the disclosure as a betrayal of confidence — both {EMPLOYER} relations and the scrip stipends suffer
If the plot is real and the plotters adapt, the school has effectively published its own warning to them
options.consequence: The school refuses to be anyone's tool, at the cost of becoming everyone's problem. The information is now known and feared by all sides, and the graduation rehearses under guard towers regardless.

costs.resource: the {EMPLOYER} stipend channel: suspended in protest for 20-30 days, with 130 trainees' pay caught inside it
costs.risk: full transparency helps whichever side was lying — and one of them was

entries.event: Graduation eve, 0220. The motor pool perimeter wire trips. 20-24 figures are moving toward the arsenal hall from the salt-flat side. In the dark, no one can tell which banner they belong to.
The unit guard detail, 8 posted, calls out a challenge. The figures halt at the wire. No shots. Both barracks begin to light up.
Cooperative and Association duty officers arrive separately, each accusing the other's trainees, each with 40-60 personnel forming behind them.
The assembly holds an emergency session by landline. Both sponsors demand the gates open, each claiming they need to 'secure' the machines against the other.
Handover ceremony scheduled: 1000, parade ground, both banners, all {MACHINES} machines on display per program.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Whoever physically holds the motor pool at 1000 holds the arsenal, the planet's defense, and the argument. Any ruling made after that only rubber-stamps who already has the machines. You have until the ceremony to produce a handover all three signers will accept, and the night is burning that time fast, one cut fence at a time.

opforSketch.composition: No conventional OPFOR. Threat surfaces: factional trainee action (squad-to-platoon scale, small arms, intimate knowledge of the school's routines — Green skills, Veteran local knowledge); sponsor security details (12-20 each, professional); and the conditional arrival of a {EMPLOYER} 'training support' detachment — 1 'Mech lance plus infantry (Regular) — whose dispatch the liaison can request but not recall. Generator should treat the school's own graduates as the primary force pool on every side of any outcome.
opforSketch.behavior: Factional action favors seizing control over fighting: grabbing, locking down, and occupying the motor pool, with actual violence as a thing that happens when the plan fails rather than the plan itself. The {EMPLOYER} detachment, if it lands, behaves with perfect courtesy — and never leaves.

forks.name: OPERATION SHARED WATCH
forks.trigger: One formation graduates and takes the arsenal handover without violence.
forks.consequence: The new formation draws its first posting: a 90-day garrison rotation under your guidance, watching the pirate corridor that made the school necessary in the first place. Both former sponsors comb every duty roster for signs of favoritism. The first real combat alarm will put the design you chose to the test.

forks.name: OPERATION RECLAIMED STEEL
forks.trigger: The arsenal changes hands by force, or graduation collapses into one faction seizing it.
forks.consequence: The assembly is the only signer still standing, and it hires the unit to recover the machines from whichever faction took them. It is a raid against your own students, on ground you taught them to defend. Every lesson you gave them is now used against you.

forks.name: OPERATION CHANGED FLAG
forks.trigger: The {EMPLOYER} drops the courtesy act. A takeover force lands within 60 days of graduation.
forks.consequence: The Association's leadership and the assembly's holdouts add up to 14-20 people the new administration will want for 'questioning.' They need to be off {WORLD} before the spaceport changes hands. The unit trained their bodyguards. It may also have to be their way out.

storyElementSeed: Two trainees from two banners share a gun-cleaning bench because the rack assignments say so. Neither speaks. At the end, without looking, each checks the other's bolt carrier, the way the instructors made them do it for ninety days, and signs the other's tag.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: One formation. One certification. The arsenal passes intact, and the honor of all three signers stays intact with it. Fail, and the school has taught nothing worth the {EMPLOYER}'s name, and the arsenal is lost or split by force.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Lock the Arsenal and Delay the Handover
resourceGates.lackingText: The unit has no secured site of its own, so the dual-key lock has to be jury-rigged inside the school's motor pool. Add 8 guard posts to the duty roster, and accept that every time the keys are used, it happens on contested ground.
The crew-pairing program runs without simulator money, so the mixed crews learn on drill time alone. That adds 12 more days of poor shooting, and those days come straight out of the range budget.

title: OPERATION FIRST KEY
skeleton: raiders must win a sealed depot from its lawful caretakers ahead of a rival claimant's column, while the methods fast enough to beat the rival poison the legitimacy that makes the prize worth holding — and the prize itself takes thirty hours to physically move
inspiration: the American-Soviet race to empty the Mittelwerk V-2 inventory ahead of the occupation-zone handover, 1945
situation:
{WORLD}, 3145. The Republic hid a fortune here: Depot Sierra, cut into a cliff face back when {DISTRICT} still got regular mail. It was sealed in 3133 and held ever since by a caretaker platoon of 28 RAF soldiers. Their warrant officer's last orders predate the Fortress wall, and he has carried them out, alone, for 12 years. The depot's inventory list is 9 years old, so treat it as a rough guide, not fact. It records {CRATED_MECHS} BattleMechs in sealed storage, more than 30 combat vehicles, and 600 tons of parts the Dark Age can no longer make. Most of the caretakers grew up here, and the warrant officer's people have married into the valley towns. {WORLD} welcomes them at every harvest festival. That fact matters more than the inventory list.

{EMPLOYER}'s regional command, working through {NPC:employer-contact}, has sent the warning order. A {TARGET_FACTION} column is {RIVAL_ETA} hours from {WORLD} orbit: about one 'Mech company with armor and mobile cranes. That report is four days old, so the exact makeup may have changed. {EMPLOYER}'s claim to this world depends on winning over its people. So the order is to liberate, not conquer. That is practical, not sentimental. Moving 600 tons of crates needs the valley's dockworkers, drivers, and cranes. None of them will work for the side that shot the caretakers their daughters married.

The key terrain problem is the cliff-face ramp. Depot Sierra's blast doors open onto one switchback road down the cliff. It is rated for 60 tons, one vehicle at a time, 22 minutes per trip down. The depot's own gantry crane loads vehicles at the top of the ramp. Even in perfect conditions, clearing all the priority inventory is a {CRANE_CYCLE}-hour crane-and-convoy job, and these conditions are far from perfect. Whoever takes the doors still has to hold that ramp for more than a day, in a slow column, while the loser decides what to do next.

The warrant officer answered the unit's messenger by signal lamp, because the depot's radios stay silent on principle. His full reply: 'Produce authority. The Republic counts its property.' {NPC:intel-source} reports that the demolition charges on the gantry crane are real, tested every quarter, and wired to the caretakers' duty desk.

objectives.primary: Secure Depot Sierra's priority inventory for the {EMPLOYER} before the {TARGET_FACTION} column can contest or claim it. Priority inventory means the {CRATED_MECHS} crated BattleMechs and the fire-control stores.
objectives.secondary: Resolve the caretaker problem without killing any of them. Try to win their cooperation first, a negotiated stand-aside second, and bloodless force only as a last resort.
objectives.bonus: Keep the depot building and its gantry crane intact all the way through extraction. The cliff facility is worth a garrison contract to whoever governs {WORLD} next.

complications.name: The Caretakers Are Locally Loved
complications.text: The 28 caretakers have gone 12 years unpaid, married into the valley, and won its loyalty. They are three things at once: the lock on the door, the conscience of the valley, and the only people who know which crate holds what.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If either side kills any caretakers, the valley's workers refuse to help that side. With no dockworkers, drivers, or crane operators, extraction time triples. If the caretakers help willingly, their knowledge of the inventory cuts extraction time from {CRANE_CYCLE} hours to {CRANE_CYCLE} minus 8.

complications.name: The Nine-Year-Old Inventory List
complications.text: Nobody outside the blast doors has seen the real inventory since 3136. Local market activity hints that the caretakers may have quietly sold off some stock, but that is unconfirmed. After 12 years of their maintenance, scavenging, and possible sales, the prize could be worth a lot or very little. Plan for a wide range, not a fixed haul.
complications.mechanicalEffect: When the doors open, the game rolls the real inventory: 60 to 100 percent of the listed 'Mechs are actually there and crated. Whatever turns up changes what is worth loading first, so the crews have to update the loading plan on the fly.

complications.name: The Demolition Desk
complications.text: Nothing heavy leaves the depot quickly without the gantry crane. That crane is wired to blow, with the trigger at the caretakers' duty desk, and they have tested it every quarter for 12 years. The warrant officer's orders are to deny Republic property to anyone without authority.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any attempt to force the doors gives the caretaker commander 3 minutes to decide whether to blow the crane. If the crane is destroyed, extraction jumps from {CRANE_CYCLE} hours to 9 to 12 days. That is far too long to win the race.

decisionPoints.name: Dealing With the Warrant Officer
decisionPoints.context: 'Produce authority.' The Republic that gave him his orders cannot back anyone's claim now, and he knows that better than either House does. You have {RIVAL_ETA} hours until the rival arrives, and clearing the ramp takes more than a day on top of that. Winning this one man over matters more than beating the column.

options.title: Produce a Forged Transfer Order
advantages: A well-made forged Republic transfer order gives the warrant officer what 12 years of silence never did: orders to hand over the depot
It is the fastest bloodless option. The caretakers cooperate fully and share what they know about the inventory
The valley sees what looks like a legal handover, which is exactly the image {EMPLOYER}'s claim needs
disadvantages: The forgery will be checked against real records sooner or later. The warrant officer trades signal-lamp letters with 2 other caretaker posts
Once it fails that check, {EMPLOYER}'s claim to {WORLD} is stained for good by a forged document
Every caretaker who cooperated is implicated after the fact, and they will know who set them up
options.consequence: The door opens within hours, but on a lie that will surface someday. The extraction runs at full speed while nobody can check the paperwork. The Dark Age is slow, so that check takes a long time to arrive. It will arrive eventually.

costs.resource: {EMPLOYER}'s good name on {WORLD}, borrowed against the day the forgery is found out, which is roughly 2 to 4 courier round trips away
costs.risk: the warrant officer has 12 years of real Republic paperwork to check the signatures against, and nothing but time to do it

options.title: Make an Honest Offer
advantages: An open offer to the caretakers: {EMPLOYER} commissions for all of them, a guaranteed depot garrison posting, and back pay for the missing years. That is relief with honor, not a forged paper
If they accept, their help is genuine and lasting. It cuts 8 hours off the crane plan and leaves a ready-made garrison behind
The valley then tells the story {EMPLOYER} wants told, for good
disadvantages: Talking eats 10 to 20 hours of the {RIVAL_ETA}-hour window, and it may still fail
The warrant officer may simply say no. His orders name the Republic, not whichever House is politest at the door
If he refuses after an honest offer, the unit has just told the depot exactly what it wants and exactly when the rival arrives
options.consequence: The race now rides on one man's sense of duty. If he accepts, the unit wins everything cleanly. If he refuses, the unit has burned hours and warned the defenders. Either way, the answer takes hours this operation may not be able to spare.

costs.resource: 10 to 20 hours of a {RIVAL_ETA}-hour race, spent at the negotiating table
costs.risk: an honest refusal leaves the depot warned, dug in, and 20 hours closer to the rival's arrival

options.title: Breach Before the Rival Arrives
advantages: Jam their comms, blow the secondary vehicle door, and get infantry inside before the duty desk can react. The plan is to beat the demolition charges by pure speed
It needs no persuasion, no paperwork, and no old soldier's conscience
It buys the most extraction time. Every hour not spent talking is an hour of crane time gained
disadvantages: The caretakers get a 3-minute window to blow the crane, and the breaching crews cannot stop them. Whether the crane survives comes down to a die roll
Caretaker deaths are likely, and they cost the unit the valley's labor, {EMPLOYER}'s liberation brief, and the cooperative loading plan
Even with nobody killed, the story is armed strangers blowing doors guarded by the valley's harvest-festival neighbors
options.consequence: The door falls in 40 minutes, or the crane falls in 3. The unit gets whatever is behind it: maybe a fortune in crated 'Mechs, maybe a wrecked crane. Either way, {TARGET_FACTION} political officers get to broadcast their version of events in the valley square.

costs.resource: the liberation brief, spent the moment the charges go off and salvageable only through flawless execution
costs.risk: a 3-minute window to blow the charges against a 40-minute breach, with the whole thing riding on a 60-year-old warrant officer's hand on a switch

decisionPoints.name: What to Load First
decisionPoints.context: The door is open and the crane survived, so now the clock decides. Pulling everything out takes {CRANE_CYCLE} hours, and the rival arrives in {RIVAL_ETA} hours, minus whatever the door already cost. Something will have to be left for the {TARGET_FACTION}. What the unit loads first is the whole strategy.

options.title: Load the BattleMechs First
advantages: These are the headline assets. In a Sphere that can barely build new 'Mechs, {CRATED_MECHS} crated ones make a real difference
Each crate that clears the ramp is a complete, movable, deniable asset
It is {EMPLOYER}'s stated preference, in writing
disadvantages: It is the slowest cargo per crane cycle: 1 crate per trip down the ramp, 22 minutes plus rigging time
The estimate is that only 60 to 75 percent of the crates get loaded before the rival arrives. The rest sit rigged at the top of the ramp as the column shows up
options.consequence: {EMPLOYER} takes the most valuable assets and gives up the rest. Any 'Mechs still rigged at the ramp head when the fighting starts become part of the battlefield. They become {TARGET_FACTION} salvage unless the rearguard makes taking them too costly.

costs.resource: the parts inventory: 600 tons of irreplaceable components left behind for the rival's trucks
costs.risk: at 60 to 75 percent loaded, 3 to 6 'Mech crates are still being fought over at the ramp head when the rival arrives

options.title: Load Parts and Fire-Control First
advantages: The most value per crane cycle: gyros, actuators, and fire-control cores, the parts no Dark Age factory can still make
All the priority parts can be pulled out inside the safe window with 4 hours to spare
It also guts the rival's salvage. Crated 'Mechs without a steady supply of these parts are nearly impossible to keep running
disadvantages: It leaves most or all of the {CRATED_MECHS} 'Mechs for the column, so in public it looks like a {TARGET_FACTION} win no matter what the real value adds up to
{EMPLOYER} clearly wanted the 'Mechs, and explaining why the parts were worth more will be a hard sell in an {EMPLOYER} court
options.consequence: This is the quiet professional's choice. {EMPLOYER} takes the parts that keep 'Mechs running and leaves the trophies behind. Within 5 years, every {TARGET_FACTION} machine from this depot is grounded for lack of parts. But for all 5 of those years, the propaganda images of {TARGET_FACTION} colors on captured crates belong to the other side.

costs.resource: the public win, given up along with the crated 'Mechs, and later answered for in an {EMPLOYER} court
costs.risk: being strategically right and visibly beaten in the same operation

options.title: Load Nothing — Hold the Depot Instead
advantages: The cliff is a fortress: one 60-ton ramp, prepared positions, and now a fully stocked arsenal behind the defense
It turns the raid into a defense the {TARGET_FACTION} column is too small to break. A 'Mech company cannot storm a depot one vehicle at a time up a cliff road
If the follow-on battalion named in the last courier digest actually sails, {EMPLOYER} keeps the whole depot
disadvantages: That follow-on report is 12 days old, cannot be checked, and is the entire basis of the plan
The unit has to fortify a cliff with only {RIVAL_ETA} hours of warning and no idea how long the siege will last
If the battalion never comes, this choice has traded the salvage for a siege and ends up with neither
options.consequence: This is the boldest bet on the table: keep everything by moving nothing, on the strength of a 12-day-old report. The {TARGET_FACTION} column arrives to find the door shut and a House flag flying on the cliff. What happens next depends entirely on whether that report was true.

costs.resource: the extraction window, spent on fortifying instead, and gone for good once the column lands
costs.risk: the whole operation rides on a follow-on report already 12 days old, in a Sphere where intelligence goes stale fast

entries.event: Alarm. Ground optical watch confirms {TARGET_FACTION} DropShips in {WORLD} orbit. They are committed to their descent and should land at the flats, 110 km southeast.
{TARGET_FACTION} column grounded and rolling: 'Mech company, armor escort, crane tractors. Road speed projection 28-34 km/h.

A {TARGET_FACTION} herald reaches the cliff approaches under a parley flag. Their recorded offer to the caretakers is {TARGET_FACTION} commissions, built the same way as any {EMPLOYER} offer already made.
The column closes to artillery range of the ramp head. It can now watch the loading, and it starts shelling convoy movement if the political officers allow it.
The full column is deployed against the cliff. Anything still on the ramp or rigged at the crane head is now contested property.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: At T+{RIVAL_ETA}:00 the rival's guns reach the ramp and the extraction stops wherever it stands. Every crate that is below the cliff and rolling west by then belongs to {EMPLOYER}. Everything still above that line is contested, and the people contesting it have a 'Mech company, crane tractors, and political officers who brought cameras for exactly this moment.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} expeditionary column: 1 BattleMech company (Regular, with a Veteran command lance), 1 armor company including engineering and crane vehicles, 1 jump-infantry platoon, organic short-range artillery. Caretaker platoon: 28 RAF personnel (Veteran in their own corridors, Green in the open), fixed defenses at the door, demolition initiative. Generator should keep the two OPFORs doctrinally separate — they share no command and may end up shooting at each other.
opforSketch.behavior: The column races, then besieges: fast to the cliff, a show of parley for the cameras, then steady pressure on the ramp as the depot's only route in and out. It will not assault prepared positions up a one-lane cliff road unless it sees the prize starting to leave. The caretakers defend the doorway and the crane, not the cliff — their fight lasts only the 3 minutes it takes to decide whether to fire the demolition charges.

forks.name: OPERATION SETTLED DEED
forks.trigger: Priority inventory extracted or the depot held, caretakers alive, valley labor intact.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} turns the operation into a permanent posting: a {WORLD} garrison contract built around the depot, with the caretakers as the local cadre. A {TARGET_FACTION} column is still on the planet, 110 km southeast, working out its odds.

forks.name: OPERATION SALTED CLAIM
forks.trigger: The column takes the depot, or the crane is destroyed and the race lost with it.
forks.consequence: Whatever Depot Sierra still holds is now {TARGET_FACTION} supply. {EMPLOYER}'s next job is denial: hit the inventory before it is spread out into the {TARGET_FACTION}'s own depots. It is a second raid against the same crates, but this time the cliff works against the unit.

forks.name: OPERATION CROSSED LEDGERS
forks.trigger: A split outcome: both sides extracted a share before disengaging.
forks.consequence: The {TARGET_FACTION} share heads for the landing flats and a waiting Seeker DropShip. The only chance to intercept it is the 110 km of road in between: one convoy, one escort company, and the unit's last shot at turning a partial win into a full one before the share lifts off-world.

storyElementSeed: No inspector has opened the warrant officer's office in 12 years. One wall holds requisition forms filed in perfect order. Every quarter he sent a request for relief to an office that no longer exists, and every quarter he stamped his own copy: RECEIVED, NO REPLY.

is-davion.objectives.secondary: The caretakers walk out of this with their pensions or their parole, sergeant's choice, but they walk. {EMPLOYER} does not start its rule here by burying the people who kept the lights on.

resourceGates.lackingText: The unit owns no DropShip lift. Extraction has to run by ground convoy 40 km to the {WORLD} rail spur, which adds 9 hours per crane cycle. Worse, the rail schedule is public, so the {TARGET_FACTION} column can read it too.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Load Nothing — Hold the Depot Instead
resourceGates.lackingText: This option is locked. It needs an operating reserve: 90 days of payroll and supplies in hand to sustain a siege. March command will reimburse it, but only at courier speed, which means long after the siege is over.

title: OPERATION CLOSING BELL
skeleton: raiders must lift a weapons consignment out of a grey-market sanctuary whose peace bond is also their own livelihood, on behalf of an employer whose identity — and therefore the raid's true purpose and payment — cannot be verified until weeks after the shooting is over
inspiration: the post-Soviet arsenal bazaar — laundered weapons lots and cutout buyers, 1990s
situation:
{WORLD}, 3151. The mercenary hiring hall survived the Blackout the way a pawnshop survives a depression: busier, harder, and less interested in asking questions. The quarterly Exchange auction is the Inner Sphere's polite lie. It sells salvaged 'Mechs with faked ownership records, under a peace bond the Exchange wardens enforce without mercy, inside the walled trade quarter. Lot 31 is the main event: {LOT_MECHS} refurbished BattleMechs, ex-Republic under their new paint, plus crated fire-control cores, at a minimum price of 4.1 million C-bills. The ownership papers are flawless, which on {WORLD} just means they were expensive to forge.

{EMPLOYER} says it is a buying agency for a Successor House. The introduction came through {NPC:employer-contact}, a broker who has been reliable until now. The agency wants Lot 31 pulled off the market before its expected buyer can collect it. The employer's brief names that buyer as an agent for {TARGET_FACTION}'s auxiliaries, but that comes only from the employer's own file, so treat it as a guess, not fact. The employer's credentials are a signed, encrypted letter of engagement and a 30 percent advance in hard currency, already paid. The other 70 percent rides on a letter of credit drawn on an off-world bank. A courier can only confirm that letter in {CREDIT_CHECK} days, and that is {CREDIT_CHECK} days longer than the auction allows. The unit sees three real possibilities. The employer is exactly what it claims. Or the employer is a rival bidder using the unit to crash the price. Or the employer is the lot's original owner, stealing back what the launderers took. The contract reads the same in all three cases. The payment does not.

The key terrain problem is the trade quarter itself. It is a walled 40-hectare compound with 2 gates, the Pedestrian Arch and the Hauler Gate. Every lot leaves only on warden-scheduled flatbeds through the Hauler Gate. Inside the walls, the peace bond is absolute: no weapon may be fired, ever. It is enforced by 200 Exchange wardens whose other job is keeping the blacklist. {WORLD} is the unit's hiring floor, its bank, and its parts market. Breaking the peace bond does not just end this contract. It gets the unit banned from {WORLD} for good.

The auction sets the clock: {TRANSFER_WINDOW} hours from the winning bid to the buyer's departure window. At that point Lot 31 rides warden flatbeds to the spaceport and is gone, past the reach of anyone whose problems stay on the ground.

objectives.primary: Take Lot 31 out of the buyer's hands between the hammer and boost, and deliver it to the employer's chosen handover point. Lot 31 is all {LOT_MECHS} 'Mechs plus the fire-control cores.
objectives.secondary: Keep the quarter's peace bond unbroken by anything that traces back to the unit. That means no weapon fired inside the walls, no warden hurt, and no blacklist.
objectives.bonus: Find out who the employer really is before the final delivery, and get proof. If the unit is being used, it has not yet named its price for that.

complications.name: The Peace Bond
complications.text: Inside the walls, the wardens' law is absolute, and breaking it ends careers. A blacklisted unit cannot hire, bank, or repair on {WORLD}, and {WORLD} is the unit's home base.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If any weapon fired or warden killed inside the quarter is traced to the unit, blacklist proceedings begin. That is a campaign-level penalty that follows the unit into future contracts. Deniable acts roll to see whether they get traced, and inside the walls nothing is ever fully untraceable.

complications.name: The Unverifiable 70 Percent
complications.text: The 70 percent completion payment is a letter of credit that nobody can check for {CREDIT_CHECK} days. If it turns out to be worthless, the unit will have stolen {LOT_MECHS} 'Mechs for just a 30 percent fee, and made enemies worth far more than that.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Whether the payment is real stays unknown until {CREDIT_CHECK} days after delivery. Until then, the unit pays every operating expense out of its own pocket. Options that cost more dig a deeper hole if the credit turns out to be fake.

complications.name: The Buyer Is Real
complications.text: Whatever the employer turns out to be, the buyer's escort is confirmed real: 8 contracted security riders. If the {TARGET_FACTION} file is accurate, add a {TARGET_FACTION} liaison who answers robbery with force, not a lawsuit.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The buyer's escort strength is confirmed when the lot is sold. If the {TARGET_FACTION} connection is real, the pursuit after the raid grows from commercial to military on the campaign layer. That means a hunting party with {TARGET_FACTION} equipment instead of just bounty notices.

decisionPoints.name: Where to Take the Lot
decisionPoints.context: Three windows exist between the winning bid and the buyer's departure: inside the walls, at the gate, and on the road. The peace bond, the wardens, and the buyer's escort each control a different one.

options.title: Before the Auction — Just Buy It
advantages: No raid at all. Outbid the buyer with the employer's escrow money and walk Lot 31 out legally on warden flatbeds
The peace bond now protects the unit instead of limiting it
The buyer's escort has no answer to this. Nobody can act on simply losing an auction
disadvantages: Bidding means posting a 205,000 C-bill deposit from the unit's own funds, backed by an employer credit line nobody can confirm for {CREDIT_CHECK} days
If the credit is fake, the unit is the bidder who defaulted: deposit gone, blacklist proceedings, and the lot goes to the buyer anyway
A rival-bidder employer gets exactly what it wanted, paid for at the unit's expense and risk
options.consequence: The cleanest plan on paper depends on the one thing the Dark Age cannot give: a fast answer about whether the money is real. The unit becomes the most exposed bidder in the room, betting its place on {WORLD} on a signature it cannot check.

costs.resource: the bid deposit: the unit's own treasury, staked against an employer credit line that is {CREDIT_CHECK} days from being confirmed
costs.risk: a default turns the unit from contractor into debtor, in the one place that enforces debts with a blacklist

options.title: At the Gate — File Paperwork First
advantages: The wardens act on paperwork. A legal challenge, such as disputing the ownership history, claiming a lien, or flagging a serial-number mismatch, freezes Lot 31 in storage for a 10-to-20-day review
It buys time for the credit check and the employer investigation to come back before the unit does anything it cannot undo
It is fully legal, and the unit never visibly does a thing
disadvantages: The freeze helps anyone with patience, including the buyer's lawyers, who have deeper pockets
A forged challenge that survives warden review needs documents as good as the launderers' own forgeries
If the challenge is exposed as fake, the wardens treat document fraud exactly like firing a weapon. It is a peace-bond violation, just in writing
options.consequence: The raid becomes a lawsuit, fought at the speed of clerks. The lot sits frozen while three unverified parties spend money proving things. The unit has turned a 72-hour problem into a 20-day problem, with the same ending and more lawyers.

costs.resource: the risk of a forged document being exposed, which the wardens punish exactly like gunfire
costs.risk: the time this buys the unit is also time it buys the buyer, whose backer may simply outspend the freeze

options.title: On the Road — Outside the Walls
advantages: The Spaceport Road runs 31 kilometers outside the peace bond. The bond ends at the Hauler Gate
Ambushing 8 escort riders is a solvable military problem with a known order of battle
It cannot be pinned on the unit in the only court that matters here. The wardens police their walls, not the highway
disadvantages: Open robbery of a paid-for lot is a scandal on {WORLD} even outside the bond. Bounty notices follow whether or not anyone can prove it
If the {TARGET_FACTION} file is accurate, the escort's backer answers ambushes with hunting parties, not insurance adjusters
The unit then has to hide, move, and hold the lot: {LOT_MECHS} 'Mechs that everyone within 2 jumps will be hunting for
options.consequence: This is the military option, and its real price is what comes after. The fight is winnable in 20 minutes, but the prize is a cargo that makes the unit the most wanted address on the mercenary circuit until the payment clears, or fails to.

costs.resource: the unit's anonymity: a highway ambush 31 km from the hiring hall is deniable, but not invisible
costs.risk: success means custody: {CREDIT_CHECK} days holding the most-hunted cargo in the Sphere while the credit letter is checked

decisionPoints.name: Testing the Employer
decisionPoints.context: Three possible employers, one contract, and the 70 percent payment hinging on which one is real. The unit can proceed blind, or it can force the question — knowing that forcing it has costs of its own.

options.title: Demand Payment Converted to Hard Assets
advantages: Demand that the completion payment be converted to hard assets held in escrow on {WORLD} before the raid. That forces any honest employer to prove it can pay, right now
If they comply, the mission is funded no matter who they are, and the unit can stop caring who it works for, the old comfort of the trade
If they refuse, the unit is only out an advance it already banked and a raid it never had to run
disadvantages: A rival-bidder employer can comply too. Being able to pay does not reveal who they are
The demand signals distrust, and a genuine House cell may just re-hire a more desperate unit on a faster timeline
Re-hiring means the raid happens anyway, around the unit or against it
options.consequence: The unit builds its suspicion into the contract and lets the market answer. Whoever pays the escrow gets their raid. Whoever refuses reveals they have a problem. Either way, the unit trades the leverage of the bonus objective for the safety of being just a hired contractor.

costs.resource: the contract itself, risked on the client re-hiring elsewhere just to avoid proving payment
costs.risk: a liar who can pay passes this test just as easily as an honest client

options.title: Investigate the Broker
advantages: {NPC:employer-contact} made the introduction, and brokers worry. About 12 days of quiet work on the broker's other deals can name the real client
Knowing the client's identity turns the bonus objective into leverage over the 70 percent payment, and over whatever the raid was really for
The knowledge outlasts the contract. Whoever this is, the unit will deal with them again
disadvantages: 12 days against a {TRANSFER_WINDOW}-hour clock means the investigation finishes after the unit has already committed. The answer arrives mid-custody or after delivery
Brokers who notice they are being investigated stop working with the investigator, and that channel is also the unit's source of jobs
The answer may be worse than not knowing. Being sure you robbed a House is different from just suspecting it
options.consequence: The unit runs the raid blind and learns the truth while holding the cargo: maximum information, maximum exposure. Whatever it learns arrives at the exact moment the unit is least able to renegotiate and easiest to punish.

costs.resource: the broker relationship, and with it the unit's flow of future jobs, staked on not getting caught investigating
costs.risk: the client's identity lands mid-custody, when the unit's only options are deliver, extort, or run, and someone else sets the price of all three

options.title: Build in Deniability and Proceed
advantages: Take the contract at face value, but build the job so nothing leads back to the unit: front crews for the ambush, hidden cargo, and a handover at a drop site the unit picks
Holding the lot at a unit cache until the credit clears turns payment risk into leverage. They pay, or the unit owns {LOT_MECHS} 'Mechs at a 30 percent discount
'No questions asked' is, after all, the advertised service
disadvantages: That 'leverage' means sitting on stolen strategic cargo while three possible clients, one maybe tied to {TARGET_FACTION}, work out who has it
The cache becomes the heart of the operation, and guarding it is an unbudgeted second job
If the payment clears normally, the caution cost nothing. If it doesn't, the unit is a fence, with a fence's short life expectancy
options.consequence: Professional indifference, fully armed. The unit runs the raid as written and turns the slow paperwork into its own collateral. The lot sits hidden under the unit's guard while the Dark Age works out, at courier speed, who owes whom.

costs.resource: a guarded cache site for up to {CREDIT_CHECK} days, the second garrison this contract never mentioned
costs.risk: every day in custody, more people learn roughly where Lot 31 went, in ways the unit cannot track

entries.event: Alarm reference. The hammer falls on Lot 31. The buyer's escort, 8 riders confirmed, signs for custody, and the wardens schedule the flatbed movement.
Lot 31 staged at bonded storage in the Hauler Gate queue. The warden escort assignments are posted, and that posting is a public document.
Earliest flatbed window: convoy of 6 through the Hauler Gate, warden escort to the wall's shadow only.
Convoy on the Spaceport Road. It is 31 km and about 70 minutes, and past the wall the buyer's escort is the only authority.
The buyer's boost window opens. Lot 31 loads at the DropPort and leaves every jurisdiction that has a road in it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: At T+{TRANSFER_WINDOW}:00 the lot lifts off-world and the contract becomes impossible to fulfill at any price. The options close one by one as that hour nears: the legal ones expire first, the deniable ones last. Whatever the unit has not done by the departure window, it has effectively chosen not to do. The employer, whichever of its three possible identities it really has, will judge the unit on that.

opforSketch.composition: Buyer escort: 8 contracted security riders (Regular) on the road — light vehicles, anti-'Mech infantry kit, professional and unsentimental. Exchange wardens: 200 inside the walls (Veteran at their actual job, which is procedure), unarmored, backed by the blacklist rather than firepower. Conditional: a {TARGET_FACTION}-equipped pursuit element (Veteran/Elite) on the campaign layer if the {TARGET_FACTION} dossier is true. Generator should keep the inside-the-walls game procedural and the outside game kinetic, and never let the two blur.
opforSketch.behavior: The wardens enforce procedure with total predictability — treat them as terrain, not an enemy, until a bond violation turns them into a sentence. The escort fights as paid professionals: hard for the first 10 minutes, then pragmatically, with no interest in dying over cargo someone else insured. The conditional {TARGET_FACTION} element does not negotiate, does not stop at jurisdiction boundaries, and treats hunting the unit down as a duty it has already accepted.

forks.name: OPERATION DELIVERED GOODS
forks.trigger: Lot 31 delivered, payment cleared, peace bond intact.
forks.consequence: The employer, whoever they really were, pays a bonus to escort the lot to its true destination, 2 jumps away. On the way, the unit finally sees the cargo manifest. It answers the identity question, and the answer recasts everything the unit has done for the past month.

forks.name: OPERATION HALL DEBT
forks.trigger: Blacklist proceedings begin, the bond is forfeited, or the lot leaves on schedule.
forks.consequence: The wardens offer the only second chance {WORLD} sells: work off the sanction in the Exchange's service by hunting down another unit that jumped its own bond with a client's cargo. The unit earns its way off the blacklist by enforcing it on someone else.

forks.name: OPERATION HOT INVENTORY
forks.trigger: The credit letter turns out to be worthless while Lot 31 is in the unit's custody.
forks.consequence: The unit owns {LOT_MECHS} 'Mechs, a 30 percent advance, and the attention of three clients who each believe the lot is theirs. The cache has to hold against commercial bounty teams, the buyer's backer, and the original launderers, while the unit decides whether it is a victim, a fence, or suddenly the owner of a combined-arms battalion.

storyElementSeed: Auction morning. A rigger chalks lot numbers on 'Mech crates that carry four owners' stencils, each painted over the last, none fully hidden. The newest stencil is the cleanest lie in the row, and the rigger's chalk does not care.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Before the Auction — Just Buy It
resourceGates.lackingText: This option is locked. The Exchange seats no bidder without 5 percent of the reserve price in hard assets on {WORLD}. By Exchange rule, the employer's letter of credit is only worth what a warden can confirm, and it cannot be confirmed yet.

The unit has no secure cache within reach. Holding the lot means renting empty warehouse space through front companies, which adds 7,000 C-bills per week. Every week also adds one more landlord who could sell the unit's location.

title: OPERATION CLEAN BILL
skeleton: relief escort must carry aid into a rumor-quarantined world and carry believable proof back out, while the proof's legal validity decays on a fixed clock, its signatories' credentials are themselves suspect, and the local power that profits from the quarantine fights to keep the world sick on paper
inspiration: age-of-sail quarantine law — the clean bill of health and the lazaretto regime, 18th-century Mediterranean
situation:
{WORLD} has been dying from a rumor for 5 months. The rumor came from a courier captain who refused to dock after seeing ground crew wearing filter masks: 'plague on {WORLD}.' That single sentence is the only evidence anyone has. It is 5 months old and unconfirmed, so treat it as thin. But with no working HPG network, no one can check it, and the story has grown at every port it reached. Three neighboring systems now block all traffic to {WORLD}. The insurance market has also marked the world VOID, which means no ship can buy insurance to travel there. In the Lyran Commonwealth that market is basically the whole economy, so a VOID mark cuts the world off. Here is the ground truth, sent by the last source still writing out ({NPC:intel-source} smuggles letters at 8 times normal postage). There was a real outbreak. It was regional, spread through the water, and killed {PLAGUE_DEAD} people. It burned out 11 weeks ago. The problem is that no trusted authority can prove it is over. So two million people are not sick, but they are cut off. In the Commonwealth, losing trade and insurance kills a world just as surely as any plague, only slower.

{EMPLOYER} is a freight company that will go bankrupt on its old delivery contracts if {WORLD} stays VOID. It has put together the one thing the insurance market will accept as proof: a licensed medical board of 5 doctors. If they sign and seal a report saying the outbreak is over, the insurers will honor it. Your unit escorts the convoy that carries them: 3 DropShips of medical supplies plus the board itself. The hard part comes next. The board must take samples in 3 districts, including the valley where the outbreak started. Their signed report is only good for {VALID_DAYS} days after the first sample, and the two jumps home eat into that window. So the convoy must lift by day {LIFT_DAY} to reach the insurers' next decision meeting, which they hold once a quarter. Miss that meeting and the report expires before the next one. Then the whole job has to be run again from scratch, if the employer is even still in business.

The key terrain problem is the quay, {WORLD}'s only all-weather port. In practice the Dornbirn syndicate runs it. This smuggling ring has sold goods on the black market at 8 times the normal price for 5 months, and it knows that lifting the quarantine kills that profit. The other landing site is the plateau: safe and empty, but 60 kilometers of switchback mountain road from the people the board needs to reach.

One more problem, found in transit and known so far to only 4 people. Two of the 5 doctors lost their licenses when the college that certified them vanished behind the Fortress wall. The insurance market requires 4 valid signatures. Your unit is escorting a cure with a flaw already built into it.

objectives.primary: The board takes samples in all 3 assigned districts. Its sealed report reaches the insurers' quarterly meeting while still legally valid. The convoy must lift by day {LIFT_DAY}, no later.
objectives.secondary: Get the medical cargo to district health authorities intact and out of the syndicate's hands. If the aid reaches people through the black market, the syndicate takes the credit and sets the price.
objectives.bonus: Gather proof that the Dornbirn syndicate profited from the quarantine, in a form a planetary court can use once the quarantine ends. The employer's lawyers will pay extra for it.

complications.name: The Validity Clock
complications.text: The signed report stops being legal {VALID_DAYS} days after the first sample is taken. The two jumps home already use up part of that time. So every day you lose on the ground is a day taken off the report's life. Delay does not push the deadline back; it just burns the report's remaining days.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A countdown starts the moment the first sample is taken. Delays on the ground, waits for JumpShips to recharge, and slow travel all subtract from the same {VALID_DAYS}-day total. When it reaches zero, the report is legally dead, no matter where it is.

complications.name: The Syndicate's Profit Motive
complications.text: Dornbirn does not want the convoy destroyed. Wrecked relief ships would make martyrs and headlines, which hurts the syndicate. Instead it wants the report to fail quietly. It will disrupt sampling, scare off the doctors, and waste days. The quarantine is what keeps the syndicate in business.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The syndicate attacks the schedule, not the cargo. Expect roadblocks, dock strikes, sabotaged sampling sites, and rumor campaigns against the board. Any violence stays deniable and is aimed at costing the mission days, not lives.

complications.name: The Flawed Certification
complications.text: Two of the 5 doctors have lost their licenses. The insurance market requires 4 valid signatures, so the report can survive one bad signature. It cannot survive two, and right now it has two. Worse, not even all the doctors know about the problem.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until you fix this at the decision point, the report is one valid signature short. Who finds out sets how bad it gets. A doctor finding out is awkward. The syndicate finding out is dangerous. The insurance market finding out ends the mission.

decisionPoints.name: Where to Land
decisionPoints.context: The quay is the syndicate's home turf, but it is only 20 minutes from the first sampling district. The plateau belongs to no one, but it is 60 kilometers of switchback road from anywhere useful. Either way, the report's countdown starts the moment you take the first sample.

options.title: Land at the Quay
advantages: The port has cranes, cold storage, and roads, so you can start handing out cargo within 12 hours
All 3 sampling districts are within one day's drive
Landing in the syndicate's own port is a public signal that the districts will read as the embargo ending
disadvantages: Every crane operator, pilot boat, and dock crew works for Dornbirn, so your enemy's workforce controls your schedule
Docking at the quay puts all 3 DropShips in one place: watched, within mortar range, and open to dock strikes
options.consequence: You buy speed and pay for it with exposure. You are working on the syndicate's home turf. Every day you save is real, but the syndicate profits from every day you lose.

costs.resource: control of your own schedule: all 3 ships depend on dock labor the syndicate controls
costs.risk: the enemy runs the cranes, so a 4-day dock strike would cost more time than any roadblock

options.title: Land on the Plateau
advantages: Defensible, empty, and clear of the syndicate, so the convoy controls its own perimeter
You never have to depend on hostile labor
The DropShips sit out of reach of any realistic ground attack
disadvantages: The 60 kilometers of switchback road to the districts add 9 days of driving across the mission
Cargo has to move by truck through country made for ambushes and washouts
Landing in the mountains looks, planet-wide, like the relief mission is not sure the plague is even real
options.consequence: You buy safety with the one thing you cannot replace: days. The syndicate does not even have to lift a finger here. The mountains burn the clock for it.

costs.resource: 9 days of the {VALID_DAYS}-day report window, spent on the terrain right away
costs.risk: the safe choice is the slow choice, and this mission fails by running out of days, not by being attacked

options.title: Split the Landing
advantages: Land the board and escort lance on the safe plateau, and send 1 cargo ship to the quay as a public, price-breaking delivery
That delivery breaks the syndicate's 8-times-price black market within 48 hours and turns dock labor toward the convoy
Sampling goes ahead safely while the syndicate is busy fighting its own customers over the cargo ship
disadvantages: Your escort is split: 1 lance has to cover 60 km of gap while the cargo ship sits exposed in the syndicate's port
If the syndicate stalls the quay ship with a fake customs delay, the lift deadline arrives with your convoy in two places
options.consequence: This is the aggressive play: you use relief as an economic weapon. The syndicate has to defend its profits in public against its own customers. But now you have 2 sites to protect, and the deadline applies to both.

costs.resource: a concentrated escort: 1 lance stretched over 60 km and 2 key sites for the whole mission
costs.risk: a customs hold on the quay ship turns day {LIFT_DAY} into a choice between making the deadline and leaving a DropShip behind

decisionPoints.name: The Lapsed Signatures
decisionPoints.context: You need 4 valid signatures and you have only 3. Four people know about the flaw, and sampling starts tomorrow. Every fix costs something you are short of: time, secrecy, or the look of being impartial.

options.title: Proceed With Five Signatures, Tell No One
advantages: No delay: the schedule runs as planned and the report arrives with all 5 seals on it
The lost licenses are a paperwork problem from a college that no longer exists; the medical findings are still sound
The odds are better than even that the insurers never audit a college that no longer exists
disadvantages: If it is audited, it is not a paperwork problem: it is a fake report. That means the employer is ruined, your unit loses its bond, and {WORLD} is marked VOID again for good
Four people know, and a secret shared by 4 people across a 2-jump trip does not stay a secret for long
options.consequence: You finish on time, but the report carries a hidden flaw that only hurts you if someone catches it. In the Dark Age, no one can easily check facts, so the lie holds for now. That cover gets thinner with every jump.

costs.resource: the employer's survival, quietly bet on no one ordering an audit
costs.risk: if it is caught, this relief mission becomes interstellar fraud after the fact, with names attached

options.title: Recruit a Fourth Signatory Locally
advantages: {WORLD}'s own chief medical officer still holds a current Commonwealth license, so a valid 4th signer is right here on the planet
A local doctor who actually fought the outbreak adds credibility no off-world board can match
It costs 2 days to vet and bring them on, not 30
disadvantages: This doctor's own world depends on the finding, which is a conflict of interest the insurers may use against the report, whether you disclose it or they discover it
The chief medical officer answers to a planetary government that, in the port at least, answers to the syndicate's money
options.consequence: You fix the flaw but add a new weakness. The report gains a valid signature and a fresh doubt at the same time. Whether the insurers accept it despite that doubt is impossible to know ahead of time.

costs.resource: the report's look of being impartial: one signer now has the biggest personal stake of anyone involved
costs.risk: the conflict-of-interest rule is up to the reviewer, and that reviewer is 2 jumps away and cannot be reached from here

options.title: Send the Commissioners for Re-Accreditation
advantages: The prefecture medical college 1 jump away can re-license both doctors by reviewing their records, which fixes the flaw at its source
The resulting report would survive any audit ever run against it
disadvantages: One courier round trip takes {REACCREDIT_DAYS} days, taken straight out of the {VALID_DAYS}-day report window
After that, the trip home has only 4 to 9 days of slack for 2 jumps, and bad weather at one recharge point wipes it out
The college may review the records and still say no
options.consequence: This is doing it right, at Dark-Age speed. It is the only fix that truly solves the problem, paid for in the one resource you cannot replace: time. It only works if everything else goes perfectly, and this mission is already a long list of things going wrong.

costs.resource: one courier round trip ({REACCREDIT_DAYS} days) taken from the report window, so the fix and the deadline draw from the same limited time
costs.risk: only 4 to 9 days of slack left for the final 2 jumps, bet against recharge lines that no longer run on any schedule

entries.event: Alarm: 3 mortar rounds land deliberately long, bracketing the landing zone during the commission's offload. No casualties. It is a warning, not an attack.
If landed at the quay, dock labor stands down 'for a safety review.' If landed on the plateau, the switchback road reports its first washed-out culvert.

A rumor surfaces in 2 districts at once: the commission is here to confirm the plague, not clear it, and sampling teams will seize and quarantine people. No one can prove who started it, but it is obviously the syndicate.

First sampling window at the outbreak valley. Crowds fill the clinic: half want medicine, half are blocking what they have been told are 'seizure teams.' The syndicate has spent only 3 mortar rounds and a stack of leaflets so far.
District authorities formally ask for an escort on all remaining sampling runs. The mission now has to guard its own evidence-gathering.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The convoy must lift no later than day {LIFT_DAY}, with the sealed report aboard. The countdown allows no exceptions. A report that reaches the insurance market even one day past {VALID_DAYS} days is still medically true but legally dead, and the market's next session comes too late to save it. Two million people's access to insurance, and with it a normal life, rides on a courier schedule and a fresh seal.

opforSketch.composition: Dornbirn syndicate: 200-300 organized personnel, 12-18 armed vehicles, dock-labor leverage, 2-3 mortar teams (Green crews, careful targeting), and money — the real weapon. No 'Mechs; possibly 1-2 IndustrialMech conversions kept deniably unarmed. Crowd elements: panicked, manipulable, never hostile by default. Generator should make the syndicate's interference proportionate and deniable: its victory condition is the calendar, not the battlefield.
opforSketch.behavior: The syndicate attacks the schedule, not the people: strikes, holds, washed-out roads, rumors, and just enough violence to slow the mission without creating martyrs. It launches a direct attack only against the bonus objective — the evidence of its profiteering — which is the one thing it will take real risks to protect. If the quarantine looks close to being lifted, expect one desperate attempt against the certification itself in the final 72 hours.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN HARBOR
forks.trigger: The report reaches the insurance market valid, and {WORLD}'s VOID mark is lifted.
forks.consequence: Legal trade returns and the syndicate's profits die at the dock. Dornbirn turns into what its gear always pointed toward: armed raiders preying on the trade lanes it used to control. The first insured convoys want the escort that already knows the ground.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WINTER
forks.trigger: The report dies, whether by the clock, an audit, or seizure, and the VOID mark stays in place.
forks.consequence: The employer goes bankrupt at courier speed. Its on-planet agents, the commission, and 11 crates of test samples are now stranded in a place the syndicate effectively controls. Getting them out is no longer a relief mission and no longer pays like one.

forks.name: OPERATION NARROW GATE
forks.trigger: The insurance market grants partial clearance: one certified route covering the port, the road, and the clinic chain, up for re-inspection in 180 days.
forks.consequence: {WORLD} gets one legal trade route, and the unit holds the contract to keep it clean. That means running the inspections, securing the route, and watching a syndicate that now needs only one incident inside it to get the planet marked VOID again.

storyElementSeed: A clinic nurse signs the sample-custody form with a pen the escort sergeant lends her, then wipes the pen on her sleeve out of 5 months of habit before handing it back. Both of them notice. Neither says anything.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Get the sealed report to the insurance market while it is still valid, so the VOID mark is lifted. In the Commonwealth, trade is life, and a world cut off is one the insurers have already started to abandon. Lift by day {LIFT_DAY}. After that, the numbers forgive nothing.

resourceGates.lackingText: You only have chartered ships. The quay delivery ship flies under a hired captain who has the right to refuse to enter syndicate-controlled waters. Add an 11,000 C-bill hazard fee, and even then he can still say no.

Option locked: the college wants its fees in hard cash. The prefecture college re-licenses no one on credit, especially not for an insurance case. The request only travels if the payment travels with it in the same pouch.

title: OPERATION PAINTED WALL
skeleton: recon element must measure a garrison that knows it is watched and stages strength it may not have, while every probe sharp enough to pierce the performance risks the incident that hardens the world against the campaign the measurement serves
inspiration: Potemkin facades for the imperial inspection tour, 1787; the Aviation Day bomber-gap flyby that counted the same aircraft twice, 1955
situation:
{WORLD}, 3150. The re-formed {EMPLOYER} means to take this world back. Parliament has voted the funds, and the {EMPLOYER}'s planners have drafted 3 possible force packages. The gap between them is 11 months of campaign budget and one question: is {WORLD} to be liberated or conquered? The planners have no intelligence newer than 31 months old. The '{WORLD} Standing Guard,' the Republic-remnant garrison on record, claims a battalion with a full BattleMech company. But two defector debriefs, 14 and 9 months old and unreliable, say the truth is an understrength company with {OBSERVED_MECHS} working 'Mechs. The two sources contradict each other on the details. They agree the rest is fake: the same lance repainted in 3 color schemes and moved between bases, radio chatter for units that are only callsigns, fresh unit markings on bunkers that hold nothing but farm equipment. By both accounts, the Standing Guard's commander is very good at this. The garrison has scared off 2 pirate probes on the bluff alone.

Your unit works under {EMPLOYER} contract through {NPC:employer-contact}. It inserts a recon element to produce a verified order of battle. The timing is unforgiving. The courier JumpShip waits at a hidden jump point and leaves on day {RV_DAY} no matter what. Any intelligence not aboard it might as well not exist. The fleet sails on Parliament's schedule either way. What your intelligence changes is which force package the fleet carries, and which speech the Captain-General gives when it lands.

The political side is worse. {WORLD}'s population is the real prize. The {EMPLOYER} is selling this takeover as a homecoming, and 31 months of blackout have left the planet's loyalties anyone's guess. If {EMPLOYER} soldiers are caught on the planet before the fleet arrives, the garrison gets the one thing its bluff cannot fake: real proof of a foreign invasion. Broadcast loudly, that proof turns the very people the campaign wants to welcome against it. One defector debrief also holds a thread no one can check from off-world: {ADVISORS} personnel in unmarked field gear, drilling the 'Mech company in tactics neither defector recognized. If some third party already has military advisors on {WORLD}, then every force package in the planners' files rests on a wrong assumption.

The key terrain problem is the tablelands. The only spot that overlooks Base 2's 'Mech hangars sits across 14 kilometers of terraced vineyard, worked around the clock through harvest season. Those hangars are where the repaints would happen, if they are real. The approach to that one good vantage runs through country where every row of vines has someone in it. Harvest is also the only season with enough temporary labor for strangers to blend in at all.

objectives.primary: Deliver a verified Standing Guard order of battle to the courier pickup by day {RV_DAY}: the working 'Mech count, the true unit strength, and the theater inventory.
objectives.secondary: Settle the advisor question. Confirm, identify, or rule out the third-party presence, with evidence the planners can weigh.
objectives.bonus: Leave no trace. No fight, capture, or sighting that anyone can tie to {EMPLOYER} before the fleet arrives.

complications.name: The Performance
complications.text: The garrison fakes its strength as routine: rotating paint schemes, fake radio chatter, empty bunkers with fresh markings. Anything easy to observe was meant to be seen. The real numbers are what all the faking is meant to hide.
complications.mechanicalEffect: By default, passive watching returns the faked numbers. Only three things return the true numbers: round-the-clock watching, an inside source, or a forced response. Each of those raises the risk of being caught.

complications.name: Harvest Country
complications.text: The tablelands approach is 14 km of worked terraces, with pickers, cart drivers, children, and dogs, night shifts included. The vineyard is the only cover strangers have. It is also a 5,000-person watch network that spreads news as fast as people talk over lunch.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each trip to or from the overwatch rolls against being spotted by civilians. Each sighting adds to an alarm count. When that count crosses a set point, the checkpoint militia starts actively sweeping the terraces.

complications.name: The Value of a Provocation
complications.text: The Standing Guard cannot fake the one thing that would help it most: proof of a foreign invasion. Your recon element is that proof, walking around. To the garrison, capturing the unit or forcing a firefight is worth more than a year of bluffing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On any contact, the garrison tries to capture and record rather than kill: prisoners, equipment, footage. An incident traced to the {EMPLOYER} triggers the campaign-layer provocation track no matter how the fight goes. Escaping does not undo the damage.

decisionPoints.name: How to Count a Bluffing Garrison
decisionPoints.context: Three methods can read the garrison's true strength, and the element has the time and exposure budget for only one done properly. Each is reliable about a different thing.

options.title: The Long Watch
advantages: 21 days of steady watching over the tablelands catches the repaint cycle in the act: hangar traffic, heat from the paint shop, the same 'Mech walk showing up under different colors
Fully passive: nothing transmitted, no one approached, nothing for the enemy to catch but the unit's patience
Produces the best result: a day-by-day activity log no analyst can dispute
disadvantages: Spends 21 of the {RV_DAY}-day budget on one hillside, with harvest traffic passing below the position the whole time
Only sees what Base 2 shows. The advisor thread and the other 2 bases stay unwatched.
Two weeks of bad weather returns a confirmed nothing
options.consequence: The patient method: the most certainty about the narrowest question. The element comes home having proven or disproven the repaint cycle beyond argument. Everything it did not watch is still wearing fresh paint.

costs.resource: 21 days hidden in 2 positions in harvest country. The alarm count rises with every supply run to the position.
costs.risk: a firm answer to one question, bought with the time that could have answered three

options.title: Buy the Quartermaster's Records
advantages: A Standing Guard quartermaster, named by the second defector, will sell the garrison's real equipment records, fuel draws, and parts use for 45,000 C-bills, dropped at a set point
The records cover all 3 bases and 18 months: the whole bluff, itemized from the inside
One deal, 4 days, very little exposure
disadvantages: A garrison this good at deception may fake its books too, so the records could be the deepest layer of the same bluff
There is no way to check them. No second source on the planet can verify the records before the courier leaves.
If the quartermaster is bait, the drop point is the capture site, a provocation handed to the garrison gift-wrapped
options.consequence: The fast method: broad, cheap in days, and resting on the one question this world is built to make unanswerable. Are the records real, or a script? The planners get either everything or a forgery, and from here there is no way to tell which.

costs.resource: reliance on one source: the whole product rests on a single seller's honesty, with no way to check it inside the mission window
costs.risk: if the records are bait, the drop point is an ambush set up to capture the unit

options.title: Provoke a Muster
