advantages: A fake raider alarm, 'pirate ships at the L1 point,' planted through the harbor watch, forces the garrison to roll out whatever it really has
One watched muster is one honest count: 'Mechs that move are real, callsigns that stay silent are fakes
Decisive within 72 hours, with all 3 bases sampled at once
disadvantages: The alarm panics 3 districts of the civilians the {EMPLOYER} means to govern next spring
A garrison that musters its real strength also goes on alert, so security doubles for weeks afterward
The harbor watch will be interrogated. If the plant is traced, it becomes exactly the foreign-provocation story the {EMPLOYER} was trying to avoid.
options.consequence: The aggressive method: one staged emergency tears the bluff open and the truth rolls onto the parade ground on its own. The cost lands on the population: fear in the districts, doubled guards afterward, and a planted lie with the unit's fingerprints on it.

costs.resource: the harbor watch channel: a one-time plant, used up in the using, with interrogation evidence left behind
costs.risk: a traced plant turns the survey into the incident, wounding the campaign's whole political case by the unit's own hand

decisionPoints.name: The Advisor Thread
decisionPoints.context: Mid-mission, the overwatch confirms the defector's report: {ADVISORS} personnel in unmarked gear at Base 1, drilling the 'Mech company in movement tactics no Republic manual teaches. Identifying them changes every force package. So does getting caught trying.

options.title: Extend the Mission and Identify Them
advantages: 8 more days of dedicated coverage of Base 1 can pin down where the advisors come from: their equipment, their drill style, their mess habits. How a unit operates is as identifiable as a fingerprint.
If a third House or a Clan already has troops on {WORLD}, this answer matters more than the whole original job
disadvantages: 8 days the RV schedule does not have. The main report then misses the courier and ships on the backup, 31 days later, on a slower ship.
The planners get nothing at the session that matters and a full answer at one that may not
Every extra day raises the alarm count in harvest country
options.consequence: The element bets the campaign's schedule against its premise: a late but true answer versus an on-time guess. Parliament's clock will not wait for thoroughness. But a force package built on a wrong assumption is a disaster that will not wait either.

costs.resource: the main courier, given up for the backup 31 days later, with the data aging that much more
costs.risk: the fleet may sail on the on-time guess while the decisive answer is still on the slow ship behind it

options.title: Photograph Them and Leave
advantages: Long-lens photos of the advisors as they are, labeled, shipped with the main report on schedule
The planners get the thread flagged with evidence, on time, and headquarters decides what it is worth
No extra exposure: the element keeps its small footprint and makes its courier
disadvantages: Photos without an ID are only a 'maybe,' and planners answer a 'maybe' by assuming the worst case
The worst case means the heavy force package: 11 more months of budget, a conquest posture, the liberation speech rewritten
The one discovery that changes everything ships as a footnote
options.consequence: The disciplined answer: the mission as assigned, delivered as promised, with the biggest discovery attached as an open question. Planners answer a 'maybe' by assuming the worst, so {WORLD}'s homecoming gets armored to match.

costs.resource: the advisor question, shipped unsolved, to be answered by force-package guesswork instead of evidence
costs.risk: an unidentified 'maybe' triggers worst-case planning, making the cheapest option here the most expensive line in the campaign budget

options.title: Tap the Advisors' Transmitter
advantages: The advisors keep an off-band transmitter shack on Base 1's perimeter. A close-approach tap, one night's work, reads their communications at the source.
Their signals name their sponsor faster and more surely than any photo. An encryption system is as identifying as a passport.
Settles the thread within the main courier window
disadvantages: The shack sits inside the only base with real soldiers in it, and guarding against recon is the advisors' own specialty
A capture here is not a minor checkpoint incident. It is {EMPLOYER} operators taken at a third party's communications site, a far worse provocation, witnessed by professionals.
If the advisors are Clan, the tap risks tipping them off that the {EMPLOYER} is coming, the one warning the fleet cannot afford to give
options.consequence: The decisive method aimed at the decisive question, done in the one place on {WORLD} where the opposition is real. It comes back with a clear ID or with prisoners, and the element learns which in the dark, at close range, with little time left before day {RV_DAY}.

costs.resource: the element's 2 best operators, sent inside the only professionally guarded perimeter on the planet
costs.risk: failure here is more than a blown mission. It warns the exact party the campaign most needs to keep in the dark that an attack is coming.

entries.event: Compromise alarm: a vineyard work crew reports figures on the tablelands to the causeway checkpoint. The militia logs it and wakes the garrison's duty officer.
Checkpoint militia (2 vehicles, 11 personnel) starts a daylight sweep of the lower terraces. It is routine, not urgent. The garrison's real speed is not yet in play.

The Standing Guard quick-reaction force forms up at Base 2. This is where the bluff cracks: what actually rolls out, in what paint, at what speed, is the most honest count the element will ever get. Get the cameras going.
The sweep line reaches the overwatch ridge. The garrison is clearly trying to capture, not kill: nets, restraints, camera teams. It wants prisoners and evidence, not bodies.
Coastal extraction window: boat pickup at the shingle, 40 minutes of slack, then it is gone.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The courier leaves the hidden jump point on day {RV_DAY} with whatever is aboard. Parliament's fleet then sails on its own schedule with whatever the courier brought. Intelligence that misses the courier does not arrive late. It does not arrive at all, and the force package defaults to the worst case. So the element's last spare day on {WORLD} is not really its own. It belongs to a planning cell 4 jumps away that will never know what that extra day might have bought.

opforSketch.composition: {WORLD} Standing Guard, true strength per the defectors: 1 understrength company, {OBSERVED_MECHS} working BattleMechs (claimed strength: {CLAIMED_MECHS}), 8-12 vehicles, and district militia checkpoints (Green). The bluff layer: a paint crew, a fake-radio cell, and a stock of unit markings — skilled at deception but untested in actual combat. Conditional: {ADVISORS} third-party advisors (Veteran/Elite, whose identity is the secondary objective). The generator should run two OPFOR sheets — the faked one and the real one — and reveal the real one only through intelligence the player actually earns.
opforSketch.behavior: The garrison fights its war through information: deter, stage, document, and above all capture — a captured {EMPLOYER} soldier is worth roughly ten times more to it than a dead one. It conserves its real combat power desperately because it has so little, and that scarcity is the secret the whole bluff exists to hide. The advisors, if drawn into a fight, behave according to whoever trained them — and that behavior is itself the intelligence the unit came for.

forks.name: OPERATION HOMECOMING
forks.trigger: A verified order of battle reaches the courier, the advisor thread is settled or graded, and no incident is traced to the {EMPLOYER}.
forks.consequence: Parliament buys the light package: a liberation-style landing with the unit as pathfinders on the ground it mapped. Seeing the size of what lands, the Standing Guard's commander will know how completely the bluff failed. He then chooses between staging a surrender and fighting one real battle with {OBSERVED_MECHS} machines.

forks.name: OPERATION HEAVY HAND
forks.trigger: The courier leaves with nothing, or the intelligence is judged unreliable.
forks.consequence: Worst-case planning wins: the conquest package, 11 extra months of budget, and a population met by a fleet sized for an enemy that may never have existed. The unit lands with the fleet it failed to inform, policing a resentment its own silence helped create.

forks.name: OPERATION SOUR HARVEST
forks.trigger: Element personnel or equipment are captured and traced to {EMPLOYER}.
forks.consequence: The garrison's broadcast runs within 18 hours: captured equipment on display, prisoners' faces lit for the cameras. The provocation track ignites planet-wide. Whoever is left of the element must cross 400 kilometers to the backup pickup, through districts that now believe the invasion has already begun. Officially, it has.

storyElementSeed: Through the long lens at dawn, a paint crew masks the same Wolverine's shin for the third scheme in 20 days. They work fast and sloppy at the edges. Where the tape lifts, three colors deep under the fresh coat, the machine's original kill tallies still hold the primer line.

is-marik.objectives.bonus: No incident, no attribution, no gift to the provincialists in Parliament. They voted against this campaign, and they are waiting on the record for exactly one photograph of {EMPLOYER} soldiers where {EMPLOYER} soldiers should not yet be.

resourceGates.lackingText: Option locked: the quartermaster wants hard cash at the drop. An IOU drawn on a {EMPLOYER} paymaster 4 jumps away is worthless to him on {WORLD}.
No in-country support cell, so the 21-day watch has to be resupplied by overland cache runs. Add 2 trips through harvest country per week, and each one rolls against the alarm count.
